examples.en: Check junk mail before you assume the housing office never replied.
examples.zh: 别急着断定住宿办公室没回复，先查查「垃圾邮件」。

words.enDefinition: nearly, very close to completely

examples.en: I've just about finished packing for the move to the new dorm.
examples.zh: 搬去新宿舍的行李我「差不多」收拾完了。

examples.en: The bus was just about to leave when I got there.
examples.zh: 我赶到的时候，公交「眼看」就要开了。

words.enDefinition: Very close to the inner side of an entrance

examples.en: The umbrella stand is just inside the door, next to the basket of leaflets.
examples.zh: 伞架「就在刚进门的地方」，挨着装宣传单的篮子。

examples.en: We waited just inside the building until the rain stopped and the courtyard cleared.
examples.zh: 我们在「楼里靠近门口的地方」等到雨停、院子里的人散去。

words.enDefinition: watch something carefully to keep it safe

examples.en: Keep an eye on the soup while I take this call.
examples.zh: 我接个电话，你帮忙「看着」汤。

examples.en: Please keep an eye on my suitcase at the station.
examples.zh: 在车站请帮我「留意」一下行李箱。

collocations: keep an eye on the food
keep an eye on your bag
keep an eye on the kids

words.enDefinition: To leave a space free of objects or people

examples.en: The floor was marked “Keep clear” so people could still get through the doorway.
examples.zh: 地上标着「保持通畅」，让人还能从门口通过。

examples.en: A volunteer asked us to keep clear of the gate while it was opening.
examples.zh: 志愿者让我们在门打开时「别挡在门边」。

words.enDefinition: stay in contact with someone over time

examples.en: Let's keep in touch after the exchange program ends next month.
examples.zh: 下个月交换项目结束后我们「保持联系」。

examples.en: I still keep in touch with my high school roommates.
examples.zh: 我和高中室友至今仍「保持联系」。

words.enDefinition: stay with someone so they feel less alone

examples.en: My roommate kept me company in the hospital waiting room all afternoon.
examples.zh: 我的室友在候诊室一直「陪伴」着我。

examples.en: I video call Grandma on weekends just to keep her company.
examples.zh: 我周末给奶奶打视频电话，只是为了「陪陪她」。

collocations: keep you company on the commute

words.enDefinition: To avoid making too much noise

examples.en: Could you keep the noise down while the group next door finishes its discussion?
examples.zh: 隔壁小组还在讨论，你们能「小声一点」吗？

examples.en: The sign asked visitors to keep the noise down near the smaller rooms.
examples.zh: 告示请访客在那些小房间附近「小声一点」。

collocations: ask people to keep the noise down
try to keep the noise down
keep the noise down in the hallway

words.enDefinition: To stay on the left side while moving

examples.en: The sign asked everyone to keep to the left when entering the hall.
examples.zh: 告示请大家进大厅时「靠左走」。

examples.en: We tried to keep to the left so people walking out could pass.
examples.zh: 我们尽量「靠左走」，让往外走的人能过去。

collocations: keep to the left on the stairs
a sign saying keep to the left
keep to the left of the hallway

words.enDefinition: stay level with something moving or changing fast

examples.en: The lectures move fast, so review weekly or you won't keep up.
examples.zh: 课讲得很快，每周都要复习，不然会「跟不上」。

examples.en: She walks so quickly that I can hardly keep up with her.
examples.zh: 她走得太快了，我几乎「跟不上」她。

words.enDefinition: move or progress as fast as someone or something

examples.en: It's hard to keep up with all the group chat messages.
examples.zh: 群消息太多，很难全部「跟上」。

examples.en: He walks so fast that I can't keep up with him.
examples.zh: 他走得太快，我「跟不上」他。

collocations: keep up with a fast walker

words.enDefinition: to stay calm and not get angry

examples.en: Try to keep your cool when the professor questions your citations.
examples.zh: 教授质疑你的引用时，尽量「保持冷静」。

examples.en: He somehow kept his cool during the heated group meeting.
examples.zh: 激烈的组会上，他居然「稳住了情绪」。

words.enDefinition: a key combination that performs an action faster than menus

examples.en: Learning one keyboard shortcut for screenshots saves me so much time.
examples.zh: 学会一个截图「快捷键」帮我省了不少时间。

examples.en: My professor showed us a keyboard shortcut for adding citations in Word.
examples.zh: 教授教了我们一个在Word里插入文献引用的「快捷键」。

words.enDefinition: take off your shoes with a quick movement of your feet

examples.en: You can kick off your shoes by the door before coming into the room.
examples.zh: 进房间前，你可以在门边「蹬掉鞋子」。

examples.en: It's nice to kick off your shoes after walking across campus all afternoon.
examples.zh: 下午在校园里走来走去，回来「蹬掉鞋子」真舒服。

collocations: kick off your shoes by the door
kick off your shoes and relax
kick off your shoes after class

words.enDefinition: fill spare moments with something unimportant

examples.en: I kill time in the library between my morning classes.
examples.zh: 上午两节课之间，我在图书馆「消磨时间」。

examples.en: We killed time at a cafe while waiting for the rain to stop.
examples.zh: 等雨停的时候，我们在咖啡馆「打发时间」。

words.enDefinition: to some degree but not completely

examples.en: I'm kind of nervous about presenting in front of the whole class.
examples.zh: 要在全班面前做展示，我「有点儿」紧张。

examples.en: The new cafeteria food is kind of bland this week.
examples.zh: 这周食堂的新菜「有点儿」寡淡。

words.enDefinition: press and fold dough firmly with your hands

examples.en: Knead the dough for ten minutes until it stops sticking.
examples.zh: 面团要「揉」十分钟，直到不粘手为止。

examples.en: My roommate kneads her shoulders after carrying her backpack all day.
examples.zh: 背了一天书包，室友晚上「揉」肩膀放松。

words.enDefinition: go down onto your knees on the ground

examples.en: Kneel on the rug to reach the outlet behind the desk.
examples.zh: 要够到书桌后面的插座，得在地毯上「跪下」。

examples.en: I had to kneel on the floor to look for the missing contact lens.
examples.zh: 为了找丢失的隐形眼镜，我只好「跪」在地板上。

words.enDefinition: hit something accidentally so it falls to the ground

examples.en: I knocked over my boba while reaching for the remote.
examples.zh: 伸手拿遥控器时，我把奶茶「撞翻」了。

examples.en: Careful in the narrow kitchen; everyone knocks over the spice rack.
examples.zh: 厨房太窄小心点，大家总会「碰倒」调料架。

words.enDefinition: to mark a box with words that identify its contents, owner or destination

examples.en: I used a thick marker to label a box with my room number.
examples.zh: 我用粗头记号笔「给箱子贴标签」，写上了房间号。

examples.en: You can label a box before filling it if the contents are already planned.
examples.zh: 如果已经知道要装什么，可以先「给箱子贴标签」再装。

collocations: label a box with your name

words.enDefinition: tie the laces of shoes or boots

examples.en: Lace up your shoes quickly or we'll miss the campus shuttle.
examples.zh: 快点「系好鞋带」，不然我们要错过校园班车了。

examples.en: She laced up her running shoes and headed to the gym.
examples.zh: 她「系好跑鞋的鞋带」，朝健身房走去。

words.enDefinition: unable to digest milk sugar without discomfort

examples.en: I'm lactose intolerant, so I ask for soy milk in every latte.
examples.zh: 我「乳糖不耐受」，所以每杯拿铁都换豆奶。

examples.en: Most adults in my family are lactose intolerant — it's genetic.
examples.zh: 我家大多数长辈都「乳糖不耐受」，是遗传的。

words.enDefinition: a delay between what you do and what the screen shows

examples.en: There is a half-second lag between my typing and the screen.
examples.zh: 我打字和屏幕显示之间有半秒的「卡顿」。

examples.en: The lag is so bad in the dorms that our team always loses.
examples.zh: 宿舍里「卡顿」太严重，我们队总是输。

collocations: the lag between input and screen

words.enDefinition: slow to respond, with noticeable delays between actions

examples.en: The dorm Wi-Fi gets laggy every evening when everyone streams at once.
examples.zh: 每晚大家同时刷视频，宿舍 Wi-Fi 就「卡」得不行。

examples.en: My old phone is so laggy that group video calls are impossible.
examples.zh: 我的旧手机「卡」得厉害，开小组视频通话纯属受罪。

words.enDefinition: relaxed and not easily worried or stressed

examples.en: My laid-back host dad never panics, even when flights get delayed.
examples.zh: 我那位「悠闲随和的」寄宿爸爸，就算航班延误也从不慌张。

examples.en: My housemates are so laid-back that exam weeks never feel scary.
examples.zh: 我的室友们都那么「悠闲随和」，考试周一点也不可怕。

words.enDefinition: one of the folded flaps below a jacket collar

examples.en: The club gave me a small pin to wear on my lapel at the reception.
examples.zh: 社团给了我一枚小徽章，让我在招待会上别在「西装翻领」上。

examples.en: I noticed one lapel sat higher than the other in our student theatre costume.
examples.zh: 我发现学生剧团那套戏服的一边「西装翻领」比另一边高。

words.enDefinition: The latest time people can enter a place

examples.en: The sign said last entry was at four, although the doors closed later.
examples.zh: 牌子写着「最晚入场时间」是四点，关门时间要晚一些。

examples.en: I asked about last entry because my class would not finish until late afternoon.
examples.zh: 我的课要到下午很晚才下课，所以我问了「最晚入场时间」。

words.enDefinition: continuing until a time well after the evening

examples.en: We worked late into the night to finish the group slides before class.
examples.zh: 为了上课前完成小组幻灯片，我们忙得「一直到深夜」。

examples.en: The library stayed open late into the night during the final week of term.
examples.zh: 学期最后一周，图书馆营业「一直到深夜」。

collocations: stay open late into the night

words.enDefinition: recently, during the period leading up to now

examples.en: Lately the weather has been too rainy for weekend hikes.
examples.zh: 「最近」天气多雨，周末都没法去远足。

examples.en: Have you seen Mia lately, with her new silver hair?
examples.zh: 你「最近」见过米娅吗？就是染了银色头发那个。

words.enDefinition: make soap or shampoo form a mass of small bubbles

examples.en: I could lather the soap easily in the shower downstairs that morning.
examples.zh: 那天早上在楼下洗澡时，我很容易把肥皂「揉出泡沫」。

examples.en: It was easier to lather the soap once I had wet my hands.
examples.zh: 手沾湿以后，更容易把肥皂「揉出泡沫」。

words.enDefinition: the day each week when you wash your clothes

examples.en: Sunday is laundry day, and the basement machines fill up fast.
examples.zh: 周日是「洗衣日」，地下室的洗衣机很快就排满了。

examples.en: I push laundry day to Saturday when I run out of clean shirts.
examples.zh: 等干净衬衫穿完了，我就把「洗衣日」拖到周六。

words.enDefinition: put on several layers of clothes for warmth

examples.en: We decided to layer up for the outdoor concert because it would cool down after sunset.
examples.zh: 户外音乐会在太阳落山后会变凉，我们决定「多穿几层」。

examples.en: I had to layer up before leaving the dorm for the early morning bus.
examples.zh: 一大早从宿舍出发去坐公交前，我得「多穿几层」。

words.enDefinition: spend time relaxing with nothing to do

examples.en: I laze around the apartment until noon on lazy Saturdays.
examples.zh: 悠闲的周六，我在公寓里「慵懒地闲待着」，一直到中午。

examples.en: We lazed around the dorm all day instead of doing our chores.
examples.zh: 我们「慵懒地闲待了」一整天，家务活全没做。

words.enDefinition: letting liquid or air escape through a hole

examples.en: The leaky faucet in our shared kitchen wasted a whole bucket overnight.
examples.zh: 公共厨房那个「漏水」的水龙头，一晚上漏了满满一桶。

examples.en: We reported the leaky ceiling to the landlord twice before it got fixed.
examples.zh: 「漏水」的天花板我们向房东报修了两次才修好。

words.enDefinition: rest part of your body against something upright

examples.en: Just lean against the wall while waiting for the campus shuttle.
examples.zh: 等校车时随便「靠着」墙站会儿就行。

examples.en: We leaned against the railing of the footbridge to watch the sunset.
examples.zh: 我们「靠着」人行天桥的栏杆看日落。

words.enDefinition: rely on someone for emotional support in hard times

examples.en: During finals week, I lean on my older sister for encouragement.
examples.zh: 期末周，我会在情感上「依靠」姐姐给我打气。

examples.en: It's okay to lean on friends when homesickness hits hard.
examples.zh: 想家难熬的时候，「依靠」朋友没什么不可以。

words.enDefinition: bend forward at the waist toward something

examples.en: Lean over the front desk to sign for your package.
examples.zh: 「俯身」到前台，签收一下你的包裹。

examples.en: I leaned over the balcony rail to check who was calling my name.
examples.zh: 我「探身」出阳台栏杆，看看楼下谁在喊我。

words.enDefinition: To keep enough space for people to move past

examples.en: We moved the bags closer to the wall to leave room to pass.
examples.zh: 我们把包往墙边挪了挪，「留出通行空间」。

examples.en: The volunteer asked everyone to leave room to pass between the tables and the door.
examples.zh: 志愿者请大家在桌子和门之间「留出通行空间」。

collocations: remember to leave room to pass
move aside to leave room to pass

words.zhGloss: 离开时把房间收拾整齐
words.enDefinition: To make sure a room is neat when leaving
acceptedZhAnswers: 离开时把房间收拾整齐

examples.en: The notice asked us to leave the room tidy after the weekly language exchange.
examples.zh: 告示请我们每周语言交流结束后「把房间收拾整齐再离开」。

examples.en: We took our cups away and put the chairs back to leave the room tidy.
examples.zh: 我们拿走杯子，把椅子放回原位，离开前「把房间收拾整齐」。

collocations: remember to leave the room tidy
ask users to leave the room tidy

words.enDefinition: sad because a group is doing something without you

examples.en: They kept switching to German, and I felt completely left out.
examples.zh: 他们老是用德语聊天，我觉得自己完全被「晾在一边」。

examples.en: Nobody invited her to the study group, so she felt left out.
examples.zh: 没人叫她加入学习小组，她感到被「排挤」了。

words.enDefinition: remaining after other parts have been eaten or used

examples.en: We made fried rice with the leftover chicken from last night.
examples.zh: 我们用昨晚「剩下的」鸡肉做了炒饭。

examples.en: Put the leftover pizza in the fridge before you leave.
examples.zh: 出门前把「剩下的」披萨放进冰箱。

words.enDefinition: very famous and admired for a long time

examples.en: The all-night diner near campus is legendary among students cramming for finals.
examples.zh: 校外那家通宵餐馆在赶期末的学生中堪称「传奇」。

examples.en: Grandma's dumpling recipe is legendary in our family, and nobody has the full version.
examples.zh: 奶奶的饺子配方是我们家的「传奇」，没人拿到完整版。

words.enDefinition: stretchy close-fitting trousers worn for exercise or casual use

examples.en: I changed into leggings for the campus yoga class before meeting friends for lunch.
examples.zh: 去和朋友吃午饭前，我换上「紧身弹力裤」去上学校的瑜伽课。

examples.en: She wore leggings under a long sweater on the day we toured the museum.
examples.zh: 参观博物馆那天，她在长毛衣下面穿了「紧身弹力裤」。

words.enDefinition: a sweet cold drink made from lemons

examples.en: Fresh lemonade from the farmers market is my favorite summer treat.
examples.zh: 农贸市场买的鲜「柠檬水」是我夏天的最爱。

examples.en: We sold lemonade on the quad to raise money for our club.
examples.zh: 我们在校园广场卖「柠檬水」给社团筹款。

words.enDefinition: an amount that keeps decreasing

examples.en: I eat at the dining hall less and less this semester.
examples.zh: 这学期我去食堂吃饭「越来越少」了。

examples.en: We have less and less free time together before graduation.
examples.zh: 毕业之前，我们的空闲时间「越来越少」。

words.enDefinition: disappoint someone by failing to help as expected

examples.en: I promised to help you move, I won't let you down.
examples.zh: 我答应过帮你搬家，不会「让你失望」的。

examples.en: He let his teammates down by skipping practice twice last month.
examples.zh: 上个月他两次不去训练，让队友们「很失望」。

words.enDefinition: To move or allow space for someone to pass

examples.en: We had to let someone through before we could close the double doors.
examples.zh: 我们得先「让一个人通过」，才能关上双扇门。

examples.en: Can you let someone through if they need to reach the stairs behind you?
examples.zh: 如果有人要去你身后的楼梯，你能「让人通过」吗？

collocations: move aside to let someone through
open the gate to let someone through

words.enDefinition: become less strong, said of rain or wind

examples.en: The rain finally let up, so we dashed to the dining hall.
examples.zh: 雨终于「小了」，我们冲向食堂。

examples.en: The wind let up around sunset, calming the lake surface.
examples.zh: 日落前后风终于「减弱」，湖面平静下来。

words.enDefinition: stay in bed without sleeping, often thinking or worrying

examples.en: I lay awake for two hours worrying about my scholarship interview.
examples.zh: 因为担心奖学金面试，我「躺着睡不着」，睁眼躺了两个小时。

examples.en: She lies awake replaying every awkward thing she said at the party.
examples.zh: 她「躺着睡不着」，把派对上说的每句尴尬话都回放一遍。

words.enDefinition: move your body flat onto a bed or sofa

examples.en: I need to lie down for a bit after that long walk.
examples.zh: 走了那么久，我需要「躺下」歇一会儿。

examples.en: She lay down on her bed and read for a while.
examples.zh: 她「躺」在床上看了一会儿书。

words.enDefinition: someone who wakes up at the smallest noise

examples.en: As a light sleeper, I always pack earplugs for dorm life.
examples.zh: 我「睡觉轻」，住宿舍总是自带耳塞。

examples.en: A light sleeper should face the wall, away from the door.
examples.zh: 「睡觉轻的人」最好朝墙睡，别朝着门。

words.enDefinition: a bright flash of electricity during a storm

examples.en: Lightning struck near the field, so the referee stopped the match.
examples.zh: 「闪电」击中球场附近，裁判中止了比赛。

examples.en: The sky lit up with lightning all through the night.
examples.zh: 整晚天空都被「闪电」照得发亮。

words.enDefinition: Permission to enter with some restrictions

examples.en: The notice said there was limited access to the courtyard during the afternoon event.
examples.zh: 告示说，下午活动期间，院子「通行受限」。

examples.en: I asked what limited access meant because our group needed only one meeting room.
examples.zh: 我们小组只需要一间会议室，所以我问「有限通行」具体指什么。

collocations: have limited access to a building

words.enDefinition: stand in a row waiting for your turn

examples.en: Students lined up outside the registrar's office before it even opened.
examples.zh: 教务处还没开门，学生们就在外面「排队」了。

examples.en: Line up at the second window for graduation gown pickup.
examples.zh: 取毕业礼服请在二号窗口「排队」。

words.enDefinition: made with an extra layer of material on the inside

examples.en: My lined jacket kept me warm while we waited outside the theatre after rehearsal.
examples.zh: 排练后在剧院外等候时，我那件「加了内衬的」夹克挺暖和。

examples.en: The lined skirt was comfortable to wear while walking across campus in the wind.
examples.zh: 刮风时穿过校园，穿那条「加了内衬的」裙子挺舒服。

words.enDefinition: stay somewhere a little longer than planned

examples.en: Don't linger in the shower when four flatmates need the bathroom.
examples.zh: 四个室友等着用卫生间，洗澡别「磨蹭」太久。

examples.en: We lingered in the museum gift shop long after closing announcements.
examples.zh: 闭馆广播响了之后，我们还在博物馆礼品店「流连」。

words.enDefinition: a clickable address that opens another page or file

examples.en: She sent me the link to the recorded lecture I missed on Friday.
examples.zh: 她把周五我错过那节课的录播「链接」发给了我。

examples.en: The link in the group chat expires in two hours, so open it soon.
examples.zh: 群聊里的「链接」两小时后失效，尽快打开。

words.enDefinition: gradually, in small steps

examples.en: Little by little, I'm getting used to the campus layout.
examples.zh: 我「一点一点」熟悉起了校园的布局。

examples.en: My spoken English improved little by little through daily small talk.
examples.zh: 通过日常闲聊，我的英语口语「一点一点」进步。

collocations: little by little it gets easier

words.enDefinition: a very large quantity of something

examples.en: We have loads of reading to finish before Thursday's seminar.
examples.zh: 周四研讨会之前我们有「大量」阅读要完成。

examples.en: My aunt sent me loads of snacks for midterms week.
examples.zh: 期中周阿姨给我寄了「好多」零食。

words.enDefinition: low slip-on shoes with a flat heel, often made of leather

examples.en: I wore loafers to the awards ceremony because the hall was next to my residence.
examples.zh: 颁奖典礼的礼堂就在宿舍旁边，所以我穿了「乐福鞋」。

examples.en: My loafers looked neat with dress pants at the end-of-term dinner on Friday.
examples.zh: 周五的期末聚餐上，我的「乐福鞋」配正装长裤看起来挺整齐。

words.enDefinition: the first screen you see before unlocking your phone

examples.en: I checked the time on my lock screen without even waking up properly.
examples.zh: 我迷迷糊糊地在「锁屏」上瞟了一眼时间。

examples.en: Her lock screen shows notifications even when the phone is locked.
examples.zh: 她的「锁屏」在手机锁定时也会显示通知。

words.enDefinition: lock all the doors before leaving a place

examples.en: Lock up before you leave for winter break—windows too, not just the door.
examples.zh: 寒假出门前把屋子「锁好」，不光是门，窗户也要锁。

examples.en: The last person to leave the studio has to lock up.
examples.zh: 最后一个离开工作室的人要负责「锁门」。

words.enDefinition: A key that locks or opens a locker

examples.en: I kept the locker key in my pocket until the afternoon event ended.
examples.zh: 下午的活动结束前，我把「储物柜钥匙」放在口袋里。

examples.en: The volunteer asked me to return the locker key when I collected my bag.
examples.zh: 我回来取包时，志愿者请我归还「储物柜钥匙」。

words.enDefinition: enter your password to start using a system

examples.en: Log in with your student ID to access the library databases.
examples.zh: 用你的学号「登录」，就能使用图书馆数据库。

examples.en: I couldn't log in because the portal was down all morning.
examples.zh: 教务系统整个上午都宕机，我一直「登录」不上。

words.enDefinition: close your account session on a computer

examples.en: Always log out of the library computers when your session ends.
examples.zh: 在图书馆的电脑上用完，一定要「退出登录」。

examples.en: He forgot to log out, and the next user saw all his files.
examples.zh: 他忘了「退出登录」，下一位用户能看到他所有的文件。

words.enDefinition: the sad feeling of being alone without friends around

examples.en: In a foreign country, loneliness hits hardest on Sunday evenings.
examples.zh: 在国外，周日傍晚的「孤独感」最强烈。

examples.en: Joining the campus photography club finally cured her first-year loneliness.
examples.zh: 加入校园摄影社终于治好了她大一的「孤独感」。

words.enDefinition: a shirt with sleeves extending to the wrists

examples.en: I wore a long-sleeved shirt because the study room was chilly in the morning.
examples.zh: 早上自习室有点凉，所以我穿了件「长袖衬衫」。

examples.en: I packed a long-sleeved shirt for the evening meal after our trip to the coast.
examples.zh: 我带了件「长袖衬衫」，准备从海边回来后吃晚饭时穿。

words.enDefinition: keep someone or something safe and well

examples.en: Could you look after my plants for one week in July?
examples.zh: 七月份你能帮我「照看」花草一个星期吗？

examples.en: She looked after her little cousin all afternoon while we shopped.
examples.zh: 我们逛街的时候，她整个下午都在「照顾」小表弟。

words.enDefinition: think someone is less important or worthy

examples.en: Some seniors look down on easy electives, but they boosted my GPA.
examples.zh: 有些学长「看不起」好过的选修课，但这些课拉高了我的绩点。

examples.en: My grandmother taught us never to look down on any honest job.
examples.zh: 奶奶教我们永远不要「轻视」任何正当的职业。

words.enDefinition: to feel excited and happy about something coming

examples.en: I'm really looking forward to our winter break family reunion.
examples.zh: 我特别「期盼」寒假的家庭团聚。

examples.en: She looks forward to her weekly video call with grandma.
examples.zh: 她每周都「盼着」和奶奶视频通话。

collocations: look forward to hearing from you

words.enDefinition: try to find out the facts about a problem

examples.en: I'll look into why our heating bill doubled this month.
examples.zh: 我会去「查一查」为什么这个月暖气费翻倍。

examples.en: The housing office promised to look into the noise complaints.
examples.zh: 住房办公室答应「调查」噪音投诉的问题。

words.enDefinition: have a similar appearance to someone else

examples.en: People say I look like my dad, especially when I frown.
examples.zh: 大家说我「长得像」我爸，尤其是皱眉的时候。

examples.en: Do the twin sisters in your dorm look exactly like each other?
examples.zh: 你们宿舍那对双胞胎姐妹「长得一模一样」吗？

words.enDefinition: examine things or pages quickly, one by one

examples.en: She looked through the flyers for student apartment listings downtown.
examples.zh: 她在传单里「翻看」市里学生公寓的租房信息。

examples.en: I looked through my photos from the trip last night.
examples.zh: 昨晚我「翻看」了那次旅行的照片。

words.enDefinition: find information in a book or on the internet

examples.en: I looked up the bus timetable on my phone yesterday.
examples.zh: 昨天我用手机「查了」公交时刻表。

examples.en: Look up the word in a dictionary if you're unsure.
examples.zh: 不确定的话就「查一下」词典。

words.enDefinition: admire and respect someone older or more experienced

examples.en: I look up to my track coach because he never excuses laziness.
examples.zh: 我很「敬佩」我的田径教练，因为他从不纵容偷懒。

examples.en: Younger students look up to seniors who survived the same brutal course.
examples.zh: 学弟学妹们都很「敬佩」挺过同一门硬课的学长学姐。

words.enDefinition: not firmly fixed or attached in place

examples.en: One loose screw makes the whole chair wobble during exam week.
examples.zh: 一颗「松动」的螺丝，让整把椅子在考试周晃个不停。

examples.en: My charger cable is loose, so it only charges at one angle.
examples.zh: 充电线的接口「松」了，只有摆一个角度才能充上电。

words.enDefinition: a strand of sewing thread no longer held tightly in fabric

examples.en: I spotted a loose thread at my cuff just before I left for class.
examples.zh: 我刚要出门上课，就发现袖口有个「松脱的线头」。

examples.en: The loose thread on my jacket kept getting caught in the zipper that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午，我夹克上的「松脱的线头」老是被拉链夹住。

collocations: a loose thread at the seam

words.enDefinition: stop contacting someone over time

examples.en: I lost touch with my middle school deskmate after moving cities.
examples.zh: 搬去另一个城市之后，我和初中同桌「断了联系」。

examples.en: Don't lose touch with your professors once the semester ends.
examples.zh: 学期结束后，也别和教授们「断了联系」。

words.enDefinition: a large quantity of people or things

examples.en: We got lots of free pizza at the club fair on Friday.
examples.zh: 周五社团招新会上我们拿到了「许多」免费披萨。

examples.en: There are lots of good study spots in the main library.
examples.zh: 主图书馆里有「许多」适合自习的地方。

words.enDefinition: very little charge remaining, usually with a warning alert

examples.en: My phone gave a low battery warning right before the professor called on me.
examples.zh: 教授刚要点我名，手机就弹出了「电量不足」警告。

examples.en: I carry a power bank everywhere because low battery anxiety is real.
examples.zh: 「电量不足」焦虑是真的，所以我走到哪都带着充电宝。

words.enDefinition: hair twisted into a knot low on the back of the head

examples.en: I put my hair in a low bun before the college orchestra concert.
examples.zh: 学院管弦乐团音乐会开始前，我把头发盘成了「低盘发髻」。

examples.en: Her low bun fit easily under the hood of her raincoat on the way home.
examples.zh: 回家的路上，她雨衣的帽子能轻松罩住那个「低盘发髻」。

collocations: put your hair in a low bun

words.enDefinition: containing much less fat than the regular version

examples.en: I buy low-fat yogurt for my post-gym snacks every week.
examples.zh: 我每周都买「低脂」酸奶当健身后的加餐。

examples.en: The dining hall labels every low-fat option really clearly now.
examples.zh: 食堂现在把每个「低脂」选项都标得很清楚。

words.enDefinition: a battery-saving setting that limits background activity

examples.en: I switch on low power mode around dinner so my battery survives the night out.
examples.zh: 晚饭时分我会打开「低电量模式」，让电池撑过夜生活。

examples.en: Low power mode dims the screen and stops mail from refreshing constantly.
examples.zh: 「低电量模式」会调暗屏幕，并让邮件不再不停刷新。

words.enDefinition: carry something heavy and awkward over a distance

examples.en: I lugged my winter coat and boots all the way to warm weather.
examples.zh: 去温暖的地方过春假，我还一路「费劲地背着」大衣和雪地靴。

examples.en: Don't lug the whole speaker system over; a portable one is enough.
examples.zh: 别把整套音响「吭哧吭哧地搬」过来，一个便携的就够了。

words.enDefinition: the meal you eat in the middle of the day

examples.en: I usually have lunch at the dining hall between my morning classes.
examples.zh: 我通常在上午的课之间去食堂吃「午餐」。

examples.en: We could grab lunch at the food truck park near the library.
examples.zh: 我们可以去图书馆旁边的餐车广场吃「午饭」。

words.enDefinition: the free period at midday set aside for eating

examples.en: My lunch break is only thirty minutes between back-to-back classes.
examples.zh: 我连堂课之间只有三十分钟的「午休时间」。

examples.en: Let's grab coffee during your lunch break and catch up properly.
examples.zh: 趁你「午休」的时候我们去喝杯咖啡，好好聊聊。

words.enDefinition: make a sudden forward movement to grab or reach something

examples.en: Lunge for the elevator button before the doors close fully.
examples.zh: 趁电梯门还没完全关上，「一个箭步」冲上去按按钮。

examples.en: She lunged across the desk to catch her falling pen.
examples.zh: 她「探身」扑过桌面，接住快掉落的笔。

words.enDefinition: a married woman's family surname before marriage

examples.en: The professor goes by her maiden name on all published papers.
examples.zh: 这位教授发表的所有论文都用她的「婚前姓氏」。

examples.en: I found grandma's maiden name in the old immigration records.
examples.zh: 我在旧的移民档案里查到了奶奶的「娘家姓」。

words.enDefinition: go straight and quickly toward something you want

examples.en: Students make a beeline for the free pizza table at every event.
examples.zh: 每场活动上，学生们都「直奔」免费披萨桌。

examples.en: I made a beeline for the sofa after moving boxes all day.
examples.zh: 搬了一整天箱子，我一进门「直奔」沙发。

collocations: make a beeline for the exit
make a beeline for the food

words.enDefinition: leave a place dirty or untidy after an activity

examples.en: I always make a mess when I dye my hair in the sink.
examples.zh: 我在水池边染头发的时候总会「弄得乱糟糟」。

examples.en: If you make a mess in the common room, please clean it up right away.
examples.zh: 如果你把公共休息室「弄乱了」，请立刻清理干净。

collocations: make a mess of the kitchen

words.enDefinition: to manage with something that is not ideal because better options are unavailable

examples.en: We had to make do with two chairs for the whole study group.
examples.zh: 整个学习小组只能拿两把椅子「将就着用」。

examples.en: I agreed to make do with the smaller bag for a day.
examples.zh: 我同意先拿那个小一点的包「将就着用」一天。

collocations: make do with what you have

words.enDefinition: form friendships with new people

examples.en: Joining the photography club helped me make friends outside my major.
examples.zh: 加入摄影社，让我交到了专业以外的「朋友」。

examples.en: It's easier to make friends when you ask people about themselves.
examples.zh: 多聊聊对方自己的事，就更容易「交到朋友」。

words.enDefinition: succeed in arriving or attending something

examples.en: Sorry, I can't make it to dinner tonight because of lab.
examples.zh: 抱歉，因为有实验课，今晚我「来不了」聚餐了。

examples.en: We made it to the airport just in time for boarding.
examples.zh: 我们及时「赶到」机场，正好赶上登机。

words.enDefinition: To free space for someone or something

examples.en: We put our bags under the bench to make room for two more people.
examples.zh: 我们把包放在长椅下，「腾出空间」让另外两个人坐。

examples.en: Could we make room for another chair at the end of the shared table?
examples.zh: 我们能在共用桌的尽头「腾个地方」再放把椅子吗？

collocations: move a chair to make room

words.enDefinition: check something so it is certain to be true

examples.en: Make sure the door is locked before you leave tonight.
examples.zh: 今晚出门前「确认」门已锁好。

examples.en: I made sure the oven was completely off this time.
examples.zh: 这次我特意「确认」烤箱已经完全关了。

collocations: make sure you have your keys

words.enDefinition: arrange blankets and pillows neatly each morning

examples.en: Making the bed first makes my whole morning feel more organized.
examples.zh: 先「铺床」会让我一上午都感觉井井有条。

examples.en: Room check is at ten, so make the bed before you leave.
examples.zh: 十点查寝，所以出门前把床「铺好」。

words.enDefinition: to become friendly again after an argument

examples.en: My roommate and I made up the same night we argued.
examples.zh: 我和室友吵架当晚就「和好」了。

examples.en: They argue over chores, but they always make up within a day.
examples.zh: 他们常为家务吵架，但总会在一天内「和好」。

words.enDefinition: move toward a place, especially slowly or with effort

examples.en: Make your way to the exam hall by 8:45 to find your seat.
examples.zh: 八点四十五前「前往」考试楼找好座位。

examples.en: We made our way through the packed night market stall by stall.
examples.zh: 夜市人山人海，我们一个摊位一个摊位地「往前挪」。

collocations: make your way to the exit
make your way through the crowd

words.enDefinition: colored products people put on their faces

examples.en: She puts on a little makeup before her morning classes.
examples.zh: 她上早课前会化点「妆」。

examples.en: Remember to remove your makeup before you go to sleep.
examples.zh: 记得睡前「卸妆」。

words.enDefinition: easy enough to control, handle, or deal with

examples.en: Twelve credits feels manageable now that I dropped the fourth course.
examples.zh: 退掉第四门课后，十二个学分就显得「应付得来」了。

examples.en: Break the essay into steps and the workload stays manageable.
examples.zh: 把论文拆成几步来做，工作量就「在承受范围内」。

words.enDefinition: the legal and social relationship between two married people

examples.en: Their marriage stayed strong through three years in different cities.
examples.zh: 异地三年，他们的「婚姻」依然稳固。

examples.en: In my culture, a marriage usually brings both big families together.
examples.zh: 在我的文化里，一场「婚姻」通常会让两个大家庭走到一起。

words.enDefinition: press and rub someone's muscles to relax them

examples.en: Massage your neck gently after carrying that laptop bag downtown.
examples.zh: 背着电脑包逛了一趟市区，回来轻轻「揉一揉」脖子。

examples.en: My roommate massaged my shoulders while we watched the season finale.
examples.zh: 看季终集的时候，室友帮我「按了按」肩膀。

words.enDefinition: extremely large in size, amount or degree

examples.en: There is a massive difference between high school and college grading.
examples.zh: 高中和大学的评分方式差别「巨大」。

examples.en: The library has a massive collection of online journals now.
examples.zh: 图书馆现在有「庞大」的在线期刊馆藏。

words.enDefinition: thinking and behaving like a responsible adult

examples.en: Living alone made me more mature about money and time.
examples.zh: 独自生活让我在花钱和时间安排上更「成熟」了。

examples.en: The mature way she handled the conflict impressed our advisor.
examples.zh: 她处理矛盾的「成熟」方式让导师印象深刻。

words.enDefinition: cooking several meals ahead for a busy week

examples.en: Sunday meal prep saves me during my twelve-hour campus days.
examples.zh: 周日的「提前备餐」救了我那些十二小时的校园日。

examples.en: We do meal prep together on Sundays and split the grocery bill.
examples.zh: 我们周日一起「备餐」，然后分摊菜钱。

words.enDefinition: the usual time when people eat a meal

examples.en: In my dorm, mealtime gets really crowded around six thirty.
examples.zh: 在我们宿舍楼，六点半左右的「用餐时间」特别挤。

examples.en: Try to keep regular mealtimes even when you're totally swamped with coursework.
examples.zh: 即使功课再忙，也要保持规律的「用餐时间」。

words.enDefinition: having no purpose, value, or sense

examples.en: Without real examples, those grammar rules felt completely meaningless to me.
examples.zh: 缺了真实例句，那些语法规则显得「无意义」。

examples.en: He quit chasing likes online because the numbers felt meaningless without real friendships.
examples.zh: 他不再追着点赞跑，因为缺了真实的友谊，那些数字「毫无意义」。

words.enDefinition: only average and not very good

examples.en: His grades were mediocre last term, so he cut gaming hours to focus.
examples.zh: 他上学期成绩「平庸」，于是减少了打游戏的时间。

examples.en: The restaurant had mediocre reviews, so our group booked somewhere else for dinner.
examples.zh: 那家餐厅评价「平平」，我们聚餐就订了别家。

words.enDefinition: arrange to meet someone at an agreed place

examples.en: Let's meet up at the library entrance at two o'clock.
examples.zh: 两点我们在图书馆门口「碰头」。

examples.en: I'm meeting up with my study group in the library this evening.
examples.zh: 今晚我要在图书馆和学习小组「见面」。

words.enDefinition: so good or special that people remember it

examples.en: The welcome dinner my host family cooked was truly memorable.
examples.zh: 寄宿家庭做的欢迎晚宴真是一段「难忘」的经历。

examples.en: Her graduation speech was so memorable that people still quote it now.
examples.zh: 她的毕业演讲「令人难忘」，到现在还有人引用里面的话。

words.enDefinition: a small removable card that adds storage to devices

examples.en: I put a memory card in my camera before the field trip.
examples.zh: 实地考察出发前，我在相机里装了张「存储卡」。

examples.en: Move your videos to the memory card to free up phone storage.
examples.zh: 把视频移到「存储卡」里，给手机腾点空间。

words.enDefinition: do something wrongly or make a place untidy

examples.en: I messed up the booking and reserved two rooms instead of one.
examples.zh: 我「搞砸」了预订，订成了两间房而不是一间。

examples.en: Don't mess up the labeled folders—everything is sorted by deadline.
examples.zh: 别把贴好标签的文件夹「弄乱」，所有文件都是按截止日期排好的。

words.enDefinition: not neat, with things left everywhere

examples.en: Sorry the floor is messy; I pulled out all my winter clothes.
examples.zh: 抱歉地上「乱糟糟」的，我把冬装全翻出来了。

examples.en: He's a lovely roommate, just a bit messy about the dishes.
examples.zh: 他人挺好，就是在碗筷上有点「邋遢」。

words.enDefinition: An intermediate floor between two main floors

examples.en: Our group met on the mezzanine above the main doors of the community hall.
examples.zh: 我们小组在社区活动大厅大门上方的「夹层」碰面。

examples.en: The sign near the stairs shows which rooms are on the mezzanine today.
examples.zh: 楼梯旁的指示牌标出了今天「夹层」有哪些房间。

words.enDefinition: the part of a device that picks up your voice

examples.en: The professor could not hear me until I allowed the site to use my microphone.
examples.zh: 直到我允许网站使用「麦克风」，教授才听得到我说话。

examples.en: My microphone sounds muffled on calls, so I clean the tiny hole with a brush.
examples.zh: 通话时我的「麦克风」声音发闷，所以我会用小刷子清理那个小孔。

words.enDefinition: heat food quickly using the kitchen appliance

examples.en: Just microwave the rice for a minute and it will taste fine.
examples.zh: 米饭用微波炉「热」一分钟就很好吃了。

examples.en: Never microwave that takeout box; the foil lining will spark inside.
examples.zh: 千万别把那个外卖盒放进「微波炉」加热，内衬锡纸会打火。

words.enDefinition: able to be heated in a microwave without damage

examples.en: Check that the container is microwave-safe before you reheat the soup.
examples.zh: 热汤之前，先确认容器是「可微波加热」的。

examples.en: That plastic box melted because it wasn't microwave-safe at all.
examples.zh: 那个塑料盒化了，因为它根本「不能进微波炉」。

words.enDefinition: a child born between an older and a younger sibling

examples.en: As the middle child, my sister says nobody took her photos.
examples.zh: 身为「中间的孩子」，我姐姐说小时候家里没人给她拍照。

examples.en: Middle child syndrome jokes follow my brother at every dinner table.
examples.zh: 每次家庭聚餐，「老二综合征」的玩笑都会落到我弟弟头上。

words.enDefinition: a line dividing the hair down the center of the head

examples.en: I made a middle part before tying my hair back for the workshop.
examples.zh: 去工坊前，我先分出一条「中分发缝」，再把头发扎起来。

examples.en: She moved the hair clip slightly to keep her middle part in place.
examples.zh: 她把发夹稍稍移了一下，好让「中分发缝」保持原位。

collocations: wear your hair with a middle part

words.enDefinition: food eaten late at night, usually before bed

examples.en: Instant noodles are my go-to midnight snack during finals week.
examples.zh: 期末周「深夜零食」的首选就是泡面。

examples.en: Don't expect me to join the all-nighter without a midnight snack.
examples.zh: 别指望我参加通宵学习还不带点「夜宵」。

words.enDefinition: pleasantly warm, not too hot or cold

examples.en: October here stays mild, perfect for reading outside on the lawn.
examples.zh: 这里的十月一直很「温和」，正适合在草坪上读书。

examples.en: The forecast promises a mild weekend with only light winds.
examples.zh: 天气预报说周末天气「温和」，只有微风。

words.enDefinition: to a small, gentle degree

examples.en: I was mildly annoyed when my printer ran out of ink again.
examples.zh: 打印机又没墨了，我「略微」有点恼火。

examples.en: The soup was only mildly spicy, perfect for a cold evening.
examples.zh: 汤只是「略微」有点辣，很适合寒冷的夜晚。

words.enDefinition: a cold creamy drink blended from milk and ice cream

examples.en: We split a chocolate milkshake after the basketball game ended.
examples.zh: 篮球赛结束后我们合喝了一杯巧克力「奶昔」。

examples.en: This diner's vanilla milkshake is legendary among the freshmen here.
examples.zh: 这家小餐馆的香草「奶昔」在新生中名气很大。

words.enDefinition: move slowly around a place without a clear purpose

examples.en: Students mill around the quad all afternoon during the club fair.
examples.zh: 社团招新那一下午，学生们在中央草坪「三三两两转悠」。

examples.en: We milled around the bookstore waiting for our textbook order.
examples.zh: 我们在书店「转来转去」，等预订的教材到货。

words.enDefinition: an enormous number of people or things

examples.en: Millions of people use this language app to practice every day.
examples.zh: 每天有「数以百万计」的人用这款语言应用练习。

examples.en: The video of our campus flash mob got millions of views.
examples.zh: 我们校园快闪的视频获得了「数以百万计」的播放量。

words.enDefinition: A polite request for permission to sit somewhere
acceptedEnVariants: do you mind if I sit here

examples.en: I asked the student, “Mind if I sit here while I wait for my friend?”
examples.zh: 我问那位学生：「我坐这里等朋友可以吗？」

examples.en: I asked, “Mind if I sit here?” before joining the people at the shared table.
examples.zh: 我坐到共用桌那群人旁边前，先问：「我坐这里可以吗？」

collocations: reply to “Mind if I sit here?”

words.enDefinition: very small in amount or degree

examples.en: There was minimal damage to my laptop after the small spill.
examples.zh: 打翻水之后，我的笔记本只受到「极小」的损坏。

examples.en: The move to the new dorm required minimal packing supplies.
examples.zh: 搬去新宿舍只需要「极少量」的打包用品。

words.enDefinition: very unhappy and uncomfortable for a long time

examples.en: I felt miserable during my first lonely week in the dorm.
examples.zh: 住进宿舍后第一个孤单的星期，我过得非常「难受」。

examples.en: The cold rainy weather made our camping trip absolutely miserable.
examples.zh: 又冷又雨的天气让我们的露营之旅「苦不堪言」。

words.enDefinition: giving a false or incomplete impression

examples.en: The apartment listing was misleading—that 'spacious bedroom' barely fit a desk and bed.
examples.zh: 那条租房信息「有误导性」——所谓宽敞卧室连一张书桌加床都勉强。

examples.en: My professor warned us that secondhand summaries can be misleading when citing research.
examples.zh: 教授提醒我们，引用研究时看二手总结容易被「误导」。

words.enDefinition: to feel sad because someone or something is absent

examples.en: I really miss my mom's cooking during stressful exam weeks.
examples.zh: 压力大的考试周里，我特别「想念」妈妈做的菜。

examples.en: He missed his hometown friends so much that he flew back.
examples.zh: 他太「想念」家乡的朋友了，干脆飞了回去。

words.enDefinition: fail to get off at the right bus or train stop

examples.en: I was so sleepy that I missed my stop and ended up across town.
examples.zh: 我太困了，结果「坐过了站」，到了城另一头。

examples.en: Set a phone reminder so you don't miss your stop on the way back.
examples.zh: 设个手机提醒，免得回程「坐过站」。

collocations: miss my stop on the bus
missed my stop on the subway

words.enDefinition: arrive too late and fail to board the bus

examples.en: I missed the bus by one minute and had to walk to class.
examples.zh: 我「差一分钟没赶上公交」，只好走路去上课。

examples.en: Don't stay up late tonight, or you'll miss the bus again.
examples.zh: 今晚别熬夜了，不然你又会「没赶上公交」。

collocations: miss the bus by a minute

words.enDefinition: a call that rang but was not answered in time

examples.en: I had three missed calls from my advisor, so I called back right away.
examples.zh: 我看到三个导师打来的「未接来电」，马上回了过去。

examples.en: The lock screen shows a missed call from an unknown campus number.
examples.zh: 锁屏上显示一个校园陌生号码打来的「未接来电」。

words.enDefinition: hand coverings with one section for the fingers and another for the thumb

examples.en: I tucked my mittens into my coat pockets before going into the café.
examples.zh: 进咖啡馆前，我把「连指手套」塞进大衣口袋。

examples.en: I had to take off my mittens to scan the student card at the door.
examples.zh: 为了在门口刷学生证，我得先脱掉「连指手套」。

words.enDefinition: combine different pieces in a variety of ways

examples.en: I packed three tops I could mix and match with the same trousers.
examples.zh: 我带了三件上衣，能和同一条裤子「混搭」。

examples.en: The costumes let us mix and match pieces from different years of the theatre club.
examples.zh: 戏服可以让我们把剧团不同年份的衣服「混搭」着穿。

collocations: mix and match tops and trousers

words.enDefinition: partly happy and partly unhappy about the same thing

examples.en: I have mixed feelings about graduating and leaving this city.
examples.zh: 对于毕业离开这座城市，我「心情复杂」。

examples.en: She had mixed feelings about her best friend moving closer.
examples.zh: 最好的朋友搬得更近了，她反倒「百感交集」。

words.enDefinition: neither very much nor very little

examples.en: The campus doctor told me to exercise moderately for a few weeks.
examples.zh: 校医让我接下来几周「适度」运动。

examples.en: The apartment near campus is moderately priced for this neighborhood.
examples.zh: 校园附近的公寓在这个街区价格「适中」。

words.enDefinition: a product used to help keep skin from feeling dry

examples.en: I left my moisturizer on the shelf beside the mirror in the shared bathroom.
examples.zh: 我把「保湿护肤品」落在共用浴室镜子边的架子上了。

examples.en: My roommate packed a small tube of moisturizer for our weekend away from campus.
examples.zh: 我们周末要离开学校，室友带了一小管「保湿护肤品」。

words.enDefinition: covered with mold from staying too wet

examples.en: I found a moldy sandwich behind the mini fridge during deep cleaning.
examples.zh: 大扫除时我在小冰箱后面发现一个「发霉」的三明治。

examples.en: The shower curtain went moldy, so we bought a new one.
examples.zh: 浴帘「发霉」了，我们买了条新的。

words.enDefinition: the way you feel at a particular time

examples.en: Bad weather puts me in a lazy mood all day.
examples.zh: 坏天气让我一整天都是懒洋洋的「心情」。

examples.en: She's in a great mood after passing her driving test.
examples.zh: 通过驾照考试后，她「心情」大好。

words.enDefinition: sudden frequent changes between happy and unhappy moods

examples.en: Finals always give me mood swings between panic and hope.
examples.zh: 期末总让我「情绪波动」，一会儿恐慌一会儿充满希望。

examples.en: Her dramatic mood swings during exam week worried her roommate.
examples.zh: 考试周她「情绪起伏」太大，让室友很担心。

words.enDefinition: changing moods quickly without an obvious reason

examples.en: My moody cousin can be hilarious one minute and silent the next.
examples.zh: 我那位「喜怒无常的」表哥前一分钟还笑得停不下来，下一分钟就沉默了。

examples.en: Teenagers can get moody sometimes, and that is completely normal.
examples.zh: 青少年有时会变得「情绪化」，这完全正常。

words.enDefinition: wash the floor with a wet mop

examples.en: After we mopped the floor, the whole apartment smelled clean.
examples.zh: 我们「拖完地」，整个公寓闻起来都很清爽。

examples.en: Mop the floor last so you don't walk over it with dirty shoes.
examples.zh: 「拖地」要放在最后做，免得又被踩脏了。

collocations: mop the floor with hot water
mop the floor once a week

words.enDefinition: an amount that keeps increasing

examples.en: More and more students are using the bike share program.
examples.zh: 「越来越多」的学生在用共享单车。

examples.en: I find myself checking my email more and more these days.
examples.zh: 最近我查邮件「越来越」频繁。

words.enDefinition: usually; in most cases

examples.en: More often than not, I take the earlier bus to be safe.
examples.zh: 我「多半」会赶早一班车图个安心。

examples.en: More often than not, the dining hall queues are shortest at four.
examples.zh: 食堂排队「多半」在四点时最短。

collocations: more often than not it rains

words.enDefinition: approximately; to some degree

examples.en: The two dorms cost more or less the same per month.
examples.zh: 这两栋宿舍每月的费用「大致」相同。

examples.en: I've more or less decided to take the morning economics class.
examples.zh: 我「基本」决定选早上的经济学课了。

words.enDefinition: more than the amount that is needed

examples.en: The meal plan gives us more than enough food each week.
examples.zh: 餐食计划给我们的食物每周都「绰绰有余」。

examples.en: Two hundred dollars is more than enough for the weekend trip.
examples.zh: 两百美元周末出游「绰绰有余」。

words.enDefinition: someone who feels awake and energetic early in the day

examples.en: I'm not really a morning person, so I schedule my classes after ten.
examples.zh: 我不是「早起型的人」，所以把课都排在十点以后。

examples.en: My roommate is a morning person and goes for a run before breakfast.
examples.zh: 我室友是「早起型的人」，早餐前还要去跑个步。

collocations: a morning person or a night owl

words.enDefinition: the set of things you do every morning

examples.en: My morning routine is simple: shower, coffee, and review my to-do list.
examples.zh: 我的「晨间流程」很简单：洗澡、咖啡，然后过一遍待办清单。

examples.en: A steady morning routine keeps me from forgetting my gym clothes.
examples.zh: 固定的「晨间流程」让我不会忘带健身服。

words.enDefinition: usually, on most occasions

examples.en: Most of the time I cook dinner with my two roommates.
examples.zh: 「大部分时候」我都和两个室友一起做饭。

examples.en: The gym is empty most of the time on Sunday mornings.
examples.zh: 周日早上健身房「大部分时间」都空着。

collocations: most of the time it works
most of the time I agree
most of the time during the week

words.enDefinition: the mother of your husband or wife

examples.en: My mother-in-law taught me her dumpling recipe over a video call.
examples.zh: 「岳母」在视频通话里教了我她包饺子的配方。

examples.en: Getting along with my mother-in-law got easier once we cooked together.
examples.zh: 一起下厨之后，我和「婆婆」相处轻松多了。

words.enDefinition: A light that responds to nearby movement

examples.en: The motion-sensor light came on as I walked into the empty hallway.
examples.zh: 我走进空荡荡的走廊时，「感应灯」亮了。

examples.en: A motion-sensor light above the door made it easier to read the room sign.
examples.zh: 门上的「感应灯」让房间标牌更容易看清。

words.enDefinition: having a strong reason or drive to work hard

examples.en: I feel really motivated now that I've set my semester goals.
examples.zh: 定好这学期的目标后，我「干劲十足」。

examples.en: Studying with her friends keeps her motivated before the finals.
examples.zh: 期末考前和朋友一起学习让她始终保持「有动力」。

words.enDefinition: the reason or drive that makes you want to act

examples.en: Coffee and deadlines are basically my only motivation during finals.
examples.zh: 咖啡和截止日期基本是我期末唯一的「动力」。

examples.en: Watching senior students succeed gives me motivation to keep studying.
examples.zh: 看到学长学姐们成功，我有了继续努力的「动力」。

words.enDefinition: smelling or looking so good you want to eat it

examples.en: The Friday curry at the dining hall smells absolutely mouth-watering.
examples.zh: 食堂周五的咖喱闻起来实在太「让人流口水」了。

examples.en: She posted a mouth-watering photo of her homemade lasagna online.
examples.zh: 她发了一张自制千层面的照片，看着就「让人流口水」。

words.enDefinition: an amount of food or drink that fills the mouth

examples.en: Swallow first — don't answer my question with a full mouthful.
examples.zh: 先咽下去再说话，别「满口」东西就回答我。

examples.en: With each mouthful of hot soup, my sore throat felt better.
examples.zh: 每「喝一口」热汤，喉咙就舒服一些。

words.enDefinition: to stop thinking about something unpleasant and continue life

examples.en: It's time to move on and focus on next semester's goals.
examples.zh: 是时候「向前看」，专注下学期的目标了。

examples.en: He moved on quickly after the club rejected his proposal.
examples.zh: 社团否了他的提案后，他很快「放下」并继续前行。

words.enDefinition: To shift sideways to leave space for someone

examples.en: Could you move over a little so I can sit next to you?
examples.zh: 你能「往旁边挪一挪」，让我坐在你旁边吗？

examples.en: We had to move over when more people came into the hall after lunch.
examples.zh: 午饭后更多人进了大厅，我们只好「往旁边挪了挪」。

words.enDefinition: move something to an earlier time

examples.en: The professor moved up the office hours to eleven a.m.
examples.zh: 教授把答疑时间「提前」到了上午十一点。

examples.en: Our flight moved up, so we must leave the dorm at five.
examples.zh: 航班「提前」了，我们得五点就出宿舍。

words.enDefinition: covered in wet, soft dirt that sticks to shoes

examples.en: The shortcut across the field turns muddy after every rainstorm.
examples.zh: 每次暴雨过后，穿田的那条近路就「泥泞」不堪。

examples.en: My white sneakers came back muddy from the interdepartmental soccer match.
examples.zh: 踢完院系足球赛，我的小白鞋「糊满」了泥。

words.enDefinition: unpleasantly warm and damp, hard to bear

examples.en: It gets muggy in the dorm at night without air conditioning.
examples.zh: 没有空调的时候，宿舍晚上「闷热」难耐。

examples.en: This muggy weather makes the pages of my textbooks feel damp.
examples.zh: 这种「闷热」天气让课本书页都发潮了。

words.enDefinition: to chew food steadily and often noisily

examples.en: He munched on chips all the way through movie night.
examples.zh: 电影之夜他「嚼」了一晚上薯片。

examples.en: I was munching an apple while rushing to my nine a.m. lecture.
examples.zh: 我边走边「大口啃」苹果，赶着去上九点的课。

words.enDefinition: so good that you really should not miss it

examples.en: That rooftop light show is a must-see before it ends next month.
examples.zh: 那场天台灯光秀下月收官，是「必看」节目。

examples.en: Her campus guide lists must-see neighborhoods that most tourists usually miss.
examples.zh: 她的攻略列出了游客通常错过的「必去」街区。

words.enDefinition: having an old, damp, unpleasant smell

examples.en: Leave the towel on the rack, or it gets musty in the pile.
examples.zh: 毛巾用完放架子上，堆在一起会「有霉味」。

examples.en: The laundry left in the machine overnight smells musty now.
examples.zh: 忘在洗衣机里过夜的衣服，现在「一股霉味」。

words.enDefinition: turn off the sound of a device or meeting

examples.en: Mute your microphone in the online class when you are not talking.
examples.zh: 上网课时没发言，就把麦克风「静音」。

examples.en: I muted the group chat during finals week to concentrate.
examples.zh: 期末周为了专心，我把群聊「静音」了。

words.enDefinition: a person who is a friend of both you and someone else

examples.en: A mutual friend introduced us during the first week of orientation.
examples.zh: 迎新周期间，一位「共同的朋友」介绍我们认识。

examples.en: We discovered a mutual friend while comparing our hometowns on the train.
examples.zh: 火车上聊起各自的家乡，我们发现彼此有位「共同的朋友」。

words.enDefinition: keep asking someone to do something in an annoying way

examples.en: My mom keeps nagging me to call home at least once a week.
examples.zh: 我妈不停地「唠叨」，让我每周至少往家里打个电话。

examples.en: I hate to nag, but the dishes have been sitting there since morning.
examples.zh: 我不想「唠叨」，可这些碗从早上就一直泡在水池里。

words.enDefinition: a small tool used to smooth or shape the edge of a nail

examples.en: I used a nail file after a rough edge kept catching on my sweater.
examples.zh: 指甲的毛边老是勾到毛衣，我就用了一下「指甲锉」。

examples.en: The nail file slipped behind the mirror when I set it on the shelf.
examples.zh: 我刚把「指甲锉」放到架子上，它就滑到镜子后面了。

words.enDefinition: lacking experience, so believing things too easily

examples.en: I was naive to lend money without even a text message as proof.
examples.zh: 连个短信凭证都没有就把钱借出去，我实在太「天真」了。

examples.en: New students can seem naive about rental contracts and deposits.
examples.zh: 新生面对租房合同和押金，常常显得「涉世未深」。

words.enDefinition: give someone the same name as another person

examples.en: I was named after my great-grandfather, who was a village doctor.
examples.zh: 我的名字「取自」曾祖父，他是村里的医生。

examples.en: Many campus buildings are named after the family who donated them.
examples.zh: 校园里许多大楼都以捐赠家族「命名」。

words.enDefinition: sleep for a short time during the day

examples.en: I usually nap for twenty minutes after lunch to survive afternoon lectures.
examples.zh: 我通常午饭后「小睡」二十分钟，好撑过下午的课。

examples.en: She napped on the couch while her laundry ran in the basement.
examples.zh: 她在沙发上「打了个盹」，衣服正在地下室洗着。

words.enDefinition: the shape of the opening for the neck in a garment

examples.en: I chose the top with a higher neckline because I would be outside all evening.
examples.zh: 我要在外面待一整晚，所以选了那件「领口较高」的上衣。

examples.en: The neckline of my sweater sat neatly above the collar of the jacket.
examples.zh: 我的毛衣「领口」正好整齐地露在夹克领子上方。

words.enDefinition: a person living next door or very near you

examples.en: Our neighbor waters my plants whenever I fly home for the holidays.
examples.zh: 每次我回国过节，「邻居」都会帮我浇花。

examples.en: A noise complaint from our neighbor arrived the night before my exam.
examples.zh: 考试前一晚，「邻居」还投诉了我们太吵。

words.enDefinition: worried or slightly afraid about something you must do

examples.en: I was so nervous before my first presentation in English.
examples.zh: 第一次用英语做展示前，我「紧张」得不行。

examples.en: Don't be nervous; the professor just wants to chat about your essay.
examples.zh: 别「紧张」，教授只是想聊聊你的论文。

words.enDefinition: not supporting any side in a disagreement

examples.en: I stayed neutral all winter while my roommates fought over the thermostat setting.
examples.zh: 室友俩为空调温度争了一整个冬天，我始终保持「中立」。

examples.en: The moderator kept a neutral tone while the candidates argued about parking fees.
examples.zh: 候选人争论停车费时，主持人始终保持「中立」语气。

words.enDefinition: not at any time; not once

examples.en: My roommate never touches my things without asking me first.
examples.zh: 室友「从不」不经我同意乱动我的东西。

examples.en: I never check my mailbox on Sundays because it's closed.
examples.zh: 周日邮件室不开门，所以我「从不」在周日取信。

words.enDefinition: someone who has recently arrived in a place or group

examples.en: As a newcomer to the lab, I asked endless questions my first week.
examples.zh: 作为实验室的「新来的人」，第一周我问了无数个问题。

examples.en: The club pairs each newcomer with a senior student as a guide.
examples.zh: 社团会给每位「新成员」配一位学长学姐带路。

words.enDefinition: the person living in the house or room beside yours

examples.en: My next-door neighbor knocked to share homemade dumplings last Friday.
examples.zh: 上周五，「隔壁邻居」敲门送来了自己包的饺子。

examples.en: The next-door neighbor collects my packages whenever I'm in class.
examples.zh: 我上课的时候，「隔壁邻居」会帮我收快递。

collocations: ask the next-door neighbor for help

words.enDefinition: The person whose turn comes next

examples.en: I was next in line when the volunteer took another batch of coats.
examples.zh: 志愿者来取下一批外套时，我正「排在下一位」。

examples.en: My roommate said I was next in line and pointed toward the open desk.
examples.zh: 室友指着开放的服务台，说我「排在下一位」。

collocations: call the person next in line

words.enDefinition: your closest relative, listed for emergencies on official forms

examples.en: Universities ask international students to list next of kin on enrollment forms.
examples.zh: 学校要求留学生在注册表上填写「最近亲属」。

examples.en: The hospital called my next of kin after my appendix surgery.
examples.zh: 阑尾手术后，医院联系了我的「最近亲属」。

words.enDefinition: an extremely small amount, almost zero

examples.en: I bought this secondhand bike for next to nothing at a yard sale.
examples.zh: 我在庭院旧货集市上「几乎没花钱」就买下了这辆二手自行车。

examples.en: The club charges next to nothing for its weekly yoga classes.
examples.zh: 社团的每周瑜伽课收费「几乎为零」。

words.enDefinition: to take small gentle bites of food

examples.en: She nibbled on crackers while reviewing her notes for hours.
examples.zh: 她一边连续几个小时复习笔记，一边「小口吃着」饼干。

examples.en: I nibbled at my toast because I was running late for the bus.
examples.zh: 因为要赶不上公交了，我只是「咬了几小口」吐司。

words.enDefinition: a person who regularly stays up very late

examples.en: My roommate is a night owl who codes until three in the morning.
examples.zh: 我室友是个「夜猫子」，写代码能写到凌晨三点。

examples.en: As a night owl, I do my best thinking after ten p.m.
examples.zh: 作为「夜猫子」，我晚上十点后思维最活跃。

collocations: stay up like a night owl

words.enDefinition: a frightening dream during sleep

examples.en: I had a nightmare about sleeping through my final exam.
examples.zh: 我做了个「噩梦」，梦见自己睡过了期末考试。

examples.en: Eating snacks right before bed gives me weird dreams and nightmares.
examples.zh: 睡前吃零食会让我做怪梦和「噩梦」。

words.enDefinition: only; a maximum of

examples.en: The essay should be no more than two pages long.
examples.zh: 这篇论文「不超过」两页。

examples.en: It's no more than a five-minute walk to the dining hall.
examples.zh: 去食堂走路「不过」五分钟。

words.enDefinition: having no mobile network bars on the phone at all

examples.en: My phone shows no service in the basement laundry room of my dorm.
examples.zh: 在宿舍的地下洗衣房，我的手机显示「无服务」。

examples.en: No service for two days made me realize how often I check my phone.
examples.zh: 两天「无服务」让我意识到自己看手机有多频繁。

words.enDefinition: someone who misses an appointment without telling anyone

examples.en: The tutor charges for any no-show without prior cancellation of the lesson.
examples.zh: 家教对事先不取消就「爽约」的课要收费。

examples.en: My lab partner was a no-show again this morning, no text at all.
examples.zh: 我的实验搭档今天早上又「放了鸽子」，连消息都没发。

words.enDefinition: low socks designed to stay hidden inside shoes

examples.en: I wore no-show socks with my loafers for the student society dinner last night.
examples.zh: 昨晚我穿乐福鞋去参加社团聚餐，搭的是「隐形袜」。

examples.en: My no-show socks stayed hidden even when I sat down with my ankles crossed.
examples.zh: 我坐下交叉脚踝时，「隐形袜」也没有露出来。

words.enDefinition: fall asleep briefly while sitting somewhere

examples.en: He nodded off during the movie and missed the ending.
examples.zh: 他看电影时「打起了瞌睡」，错过了结尾。

examples.en: I keep nodding off on the bus after my morning classes.
examples.zh: 上午的课上完之后，我在公交上总「打瞌睡」。

words.enDefinition: A mat designed to reduce slipping

examples.en: The volunteer laid a non-slip mat inside the entrance after it began raining.
examples.zh: 下雨后，志愿者在入口内侧铺了一张「防滑垫」。

examples.en: I put my umbrella aside and stepped onto the non-slip mat by the door.
examples.zh: 我把伞放到一边，踩上了门边的「防滑垫」。

words.enDefinition: not one of a group of people or things

examples.en: None of the vending machines on this floor take cash.
examples.zh: 这一层的自动售货机「一台都不」收现金。

examples.en: None of my roommates wanted to split the delivery fee.
examples.zh: 我的室友们「谁也不」想分摊外送费。

words.enDefinition: a warm, wistful feeling remembering good times in the past

examples.en: A wave of nostalgia hit me when I heard my childhood cartoon song.
examples.zh: 听到童年的动画片主题曲，一阵「怀旧之情」涌上心头。

examples.en: My roommate cooks her grandma's recipes out of pure nostalgia.
examples.zh: 室友做外婆的拿手菜，纯粹是出于「怀念」。

words.enDefinition: feeling both happy and sad when remembering the past

examples.en: Scrolling through old high school photos made the whole group nostalgic.
examples.zh: 翻看高中老照片，让整个群里的人都「怀旧」起来。

examples.en: I always feel nostalgic when I hear songs from my hometown.
examples.zh: 每次听到家乡的歌，我都会很「怀旧」。

words.enDefinition: too interested in other people's private business

examples.en: My neighbor is nice but nosy; she always asks who was visiting me.
examples.zh: 邻居人不错就是「爱打听」，总问谁来找我。

examples.en: Quit being nosy about my grades; that's between me and my advisor.
examples.zh: 别对我的成绩「打破砂锅问到底」，那是我和导师之间的事。

words.enDefinition: less than the amount needed

examples.en: There's not enough space in the microwave for two lunch boxes.
examples.zh: 微波炉的空间「不够」，放不下两个饭盒。

examples.en: I skipped breakfast because there was not enough time before class.
examples.zh: 上课前时间「不够」，我没来得及吃早餐。

words.enDefinition: write something quickly so you remember it

examples.en: Note down the professor's office hours before you leave the hall.
examples.zh: 离开教室前，把教授的办公时间「记下来」。

examples.en: I noted down the Wi-Fi password as soon as she said it.
examples.zh: 她一说Wi-Fi密码，我就「记」了下来。

words.enDefinition: A board displaying notices for people to read

examples.en: I checked the noticeboard for the date of the next community book swap.
examples.zh: 我查看了「公告栏」，找下一次社区换书活动的日期。

examples.en: The noticeboard by the entrance had a sheet listing the rooms open that day.
examples.zh: 入口旁的「公告栏」贴了张纸，列出当天开放的房间。

collocations: put up a notice on the noticeboard

words.enDefinition: well known for something bad

examples.en: That intersection near campus is notorious for fender benders, so I cross carefully.
examples.zh: 校门口那个路口「出了名」地爱追尾，我过马路格外小心。

examples.en: Our building's elevator is notorious for breaking down right before morning classes.
examples.zh: 我们楼的电梯「出了名地差劲」，总在早课前罢工。

words.enDefinition: much less than the stated amount or level

examples.en: My budget is nowhere near enough for an apartment downtown.
examples.zh: 我的预算「远不够」在市中心租房。

examples.en: The shuttle stop is nowhere near as close as the map showed.
examples.zh: 班车站「远不如」地图上显示的那么近。

words.enDefinition: a family unit of parents and their children only

examples.en: In the city, most students I know come from a nuclear family.
examples.zh: 在城市里，我认识的大多数同学都来自「核心家庭」。

examples.en: A nuclear family usually finds it easier to move for work.
examples.zh: 「核心家庭」通常更容易为了工作而搬家。

collocations: grow up in a nuclear family

words.enDefinition: push someone gently, usually with your elbow

examples.en: I nudged my deskmate when the professor mentioned the surprise quiz.
examples.zh: 教授提到突击测验时，我用手肘「轻碰」了一下同桌。

examples.en: Nudge the fridge door; it doesn't always close on its own.
examples.zh: 顺手把冰箱门「轻推」一下，它经常自己关不严。

words.enDefinition: unable to feel anything because something has shocked you

examples.en: After hours of waiting, I just felt numb about the results.
examples.zh: 等了几个小时之后，我对结果已经感觉「麻木」了。

examples.en: I went numb when I read the rejection email this morning.
examples.zh: 今天早上读到拒信时，我整个人都「麻了」。

words.enDefinition: existing in large numbers

examples.en: There are numerous reasons to double-check your flight details before leaving.
examples.zh: 出发前有「众多」理由需要反复核对航班信息。

examples.en: The professor gave numerous examples to make the theory easier to understand.
examples.zh: 教授举了「众多」例子，让理论更容易理解。

words.enDefinition: the panel showing calories and nutrients on packaging

examples.en: Read the nutrition label before buying granola bars in bulk.
examples.zh: 整箱买燕麦棒之前，先看看「营养成分表」。

examples.en: The nutrition label says one bowl has twelve grams of sugar.
examples.zh: 「营养标签」显示一碗含十二克糖。

collocations: the nutrition label on the back

words.enDefinition: A sign showing that a space is already occupied

examples.en: I saw an occupied sign on the cubicle door and waited by the sinks.
examples.zh: 我看到隔间门上有「有人使用的标示」，就到洗手池旁边等。

examples.en: The occupied sign turned red when I locked the cubicle door from inside.
examples.zh: 我从里面锁上隔间门时，「有人使用的标示」变成了红色。

words.enDefinition: in an irregular, intermittent way

examples.en: I've been learning guitar off and on since high school.
examples.zh: 从高中起，我就「断断续续」地学吉他。

examples.en: It rained off and on during our whole campus tour.
examples.zh: 校园参观期间，雨「断断续续」地下着。

words.enDefinition: Hours when a place or service is less busy

examples.en: We visited during off-peak hours and had the back of the hall to ourselves.
examples.zh: 我们在「非高峰时段」去了大厅，整个后半区就我们在用。

examples.en: I asked which off-peak hours would be best for our small reading group.
examples.zh: 我问我们的读书小组选哪个「非高峰时段」比较合适。

words.enDefinition: not connected to the internet or a network right now

examples.en: The study app shows your flashcards offline, which saves data on the bus.
examples.zh: 这个学习应用支持「离线」看单词卡，坐公交不费流量。

examples.en: I went offline for the weekend and my inbox hated me on Monday.
examples.zh: 周末我「离线」了两天，周一的收件箱惨不忍睹。

words.enDefinition: many times; frequently

examples.en: We often study together at the coffee shop near campus.
examples.zh: 我们「经常」在校门口的咖啡店一起学习。

examples.en: I often skip lunch when my class schedule gets really busy.
examples.zh: 课表一忙，我就「经常」不吃午饭。

words.enDefinition: belonging to an older style, not modern

examples.en: My grandmother still keeps an old-fashioned paper calendar instead of any phone app.
examples.zh: 我奶奶还在用「老式」纸质日历，不用任何手机应用。

examples.en: The diner kept its old-fashioned stools and chrome counters from the 1950s.
examples.zh: 这家餐馆保留着上世纪五十年代「老式」的吧台凳和铬合金柜台。

words.enDefinition: the first-born child among the children in a family

examples.en: As the oldest child, I helped my parents raise my younger brothers.
examples.zh: 作为「家里的老大」，我帮父母带大了弟弟们。

examples.en: The oldest child in my host family leaves for college next fall.
examples.zh: 我寄宿家庭的「老大」明年秋天就要去上大学了。

words.enDefinition: every day, regularly

examples.en: I water the lab plants on a daily basis for my campus job.
examples.zh: 作为校内工作，我「每天」给实验室的植物浇水。

examples.en: We track our expenses on a daily basis in a shared sheet.
examples.zh: 我们在共享表格里「每天」记录开支。

collocations: on a daily basis at work

words.enDefinition: following a controlled eating plan to lose weight

examples.en: I'm on a diet until the wedding in June, so no dessert.
examples.zh: 六月婚礼前我都在「节食」，甜点就免了。

examples.en: She's on a diet that cuts out late-night snacks completely.
examples.zh: 她正在「节食」，完全戒掉了深夜零食。

words.enDefinition: regularly, at fixed intervals

examples.en: The counseling center suggests checking in on a regular basis.
examples.zh: 心理咨询中心建议大家「定期」去聊聊。

examples.en: Our club reviews its budget on a regular basis each semester.
examples.zh: 我们社团每学期都会「定期」审阅预算。

words.enDefinition: usually or typically, based on calculations

examples.en: Students here spend on average two hours a day in the library.
examples.zh: 这里的学生「平均」每天在图书馆待两个小时。

examples.en: We spend on average sixty dollars a week on groceries.
examples.zh: 我们「平均」每周花六十美元买食材。

words.enDefinition: nervous and easily irritated because you expect trouble

examples.en: Everyone has been on edge since the professor announced the final.
examples.zh: 自从教授宣布期末考试安排后，大家都「紧张不安」。

examples.en: Our loud neighbors keep me on edge almost every night.
examples.zh: 吵闹的邻居让我几乎每晚都「神经紧绷」。

words.enDefinition: walking rather than riding or driving

examples.en: My apartment is close, so I go everywhere on foot.
examples.zh: 我住得近，去哪儿都靠「步行」。

examples.en: It takes about half an hour on foot from the dorm to the station.
examples.zh: 从宿舍到车站，「步行」大概要半个小时。

words.enDefinition: at the same level or standard as

examples.en: The food truck's burritos are on par with the restaurant's.
examples.zh: 餐车卖的墨西哥卷和那家餐厅的「不相上下」。

examples.en: Our department's labs are on par with any top university's.
examples.zh: 我们系的实验室「不输」任何顶尖大学。

words.enDefinition: with very little warning or preparation time

examples.en: The quiz was announced on short notice, so I skimmed my notes.
examples.zh: 测验是「临时通知」的，我只快速翻了翻笔记。

examples.en: Can you cover my cafe shift on short notice tomorrow morning?
examples.zh: 明天早上你能「临时」替我顶咖啡店的班吗？

words.enDefinition: at exactly the agreed or stated time

examples.en: The seminar starts at nine on the dot, so arrive early.
examples.zh: 研讨会九点「整」开始，请提前到场。

examples.en: Her alarm rings at six thirty on the dot every day.
examples.zh: 她的闹钟每天六点半「准时」响。

words.enDefinition: at the exact expected time, not late

examples.en: The shuttle is usually on time, but today it ran late.
examples.zh: 班车通常「准时」，但今天晚了。

examples.en: Handing in assignments on time protects your grade in most courses.
examples.zh: 「按时」交作业能保住你大部分课程的平时成绩。

words.enDefinition: one time in each week

examples.en: Our lab section meets once a week on Thursday afternoons.
examples.zh: 我们的实验课「每周一次」，排在周四下午。

examples.en: I do a big grocery run once a week to save time.
examples.zh: 为了省时间，我「每周一次」集中采购食材。

words.enDefinition: very rarely

examples.en: We go to that fancy restaurant once in a blue moon.
examples.zh: 我们「难得」去一次那家高档餐厅。

examples.en: Once in a blue moon my roommates all get home at the same time.
examples.zh: 我的室友们「难得」同时到家。

collocations: happen once in a blue moon
once in a blue moon we meet
once in a blue moon only

words.enDefinition: occasionally, but not very often

examples.en: Once in a while I skip cooking and order pizza instead.
examples.zh: 我「偶尔」会不做饭，改点披萨。

examples.en: Call your grandparents once in a while; they miss you.
examples.zh: 「偶尔」给爷爷奶奶打个电话，他们很想你。

collocations: once in a while treat yourself

words.enDefinition: one or two times only

examples.en: I've been to the new ramen place once or twice this month.
examples.zh: 这个月我去那家新拉面店吃了「一两次」。

examples.en: Honestly, I've overslept only once or twice this whole semester.
examples.zh: 说实话，这学期我睡过头「只有一两次」。

words.enDefinition: first one, then the next, then the next

examples.en: The new club members introduced themselves one by one at the meeting.
examples.zh: 新社员在会上「一个接一个」地自我介绍。

examples.en: We checked the applicants' names one by one against the list.
examples.zh: 我们把申请者的名字「逐一」和名单核对了一遍。

words.enDefinition: considering only one person's view or interest

examples.en: The article on the tuition hike felt one-sided because it never quoted a single student.
examples.zh: 那篇学费上涨的报道很「片面」，从头到尾没采访一个学生。

examples.en: Their friendship became one-sided—she always made the plans and covered the rideshare.
examples.zh: 她们的友谊变得「一边倒」，永远是她安排行程、她付车费。

words.enDefinition: a child with no brothers or sisters

examples.en: As an only child, I learned to entertain myself with books.
examples.zh: 作为「独生子女」，我从小学会用书打发时间。

examples.en: My roommate grew up as an only child, so sharing felt strange at first.
examples.zh: 我的室友是「独生子女」，一开始不太习惯和人分享。

collocations: grow up as an only child
the only child of my parents

words.enDefinition: tights made from fabric that you cannot see through

examples.en: I wore opaque tights under my skirt because we were walking back late at night.
examples.zh: 我们要深夜走回去，所以我在裙子下面穿了「不透肤连裤袜」。

examples.en: She packed opaque tights for the student concert to go with her dark dress.
examples.zh: 她带了「不透肤连裤袜」去学生音乐会，搭配自己的深色连衣裙。

words.enDefinition: willing to consider new ideas and different views

examples.en: My open-minded host family tried cooking dumplings for Spring Festival.
examples.zh: 我「思想开明的」寄宿家庭为了春节试着包了饺子。

examples.en: Studying abroad is easier if you stay open-minded about food customs.
examples.zh: 如果对饮食习俗保持「开放心态」，留学会轻松许多。

words.enDefinition: Available for anyone to enter or use

examples.en: The courtyard is open to the public even when the meeting rooms are locked.
examples.zh: 即使会议室锁了，院子也「向公众开放」。

examples.en: I asked whether the hall was open to the public during the weekend.
examples.zh: 我问大厅周末是否「向公众开放」。

collocations: open to the public on weekdays

words.enDefinition: to start talking honestly about your private feelings

examples.en: My roommate slowly opened up about her anxiety during midterms.
examples.zh: 期中考试期间，室友慢慢「敞开心扉」，聊起她的焦虑。

examples.en: He finds it hard to open up to people he just met.
examples.zh: 他很难向刚认识的人「敞开心扉」。

words.enDefinition: the core software that runs a phone or computer

examples.en: The new operating system made my three-year-old laptop feel sluggish.
examples.zh: 新的「操作系统」让我用了三年的笔记本变得反应迟钝。

examples.en: Update your operating system through settings, then restart before installing anything else.
examples.zh: 在设置里更新「操作系统」，装其他东西之前先重启一次。

collocations: your operating system is out of date

words.enDefinition: expecting good things to happen in the future

examples.en: I'm feeling optimistic about finding a part-time job before September.
examples.zh: 我对九月前找到兼职这件事很「乐观」。

examples.en: She stayed optimistic even after failing her first job interview.
examples.zh: 第一次求职面试失败后，她依然很「乐观」。

words.enDefinition: not required; you decide whether to do it

examples.en: The Thursday review session is optional, but it genuinely helps.
examples.zh: 周四的复习课「自愿参加」，不过真的有用。

examples.en: Attendance at the guest lecture is optional and won't affect grades.
examples.zh: 嘉宾讲座「可以自愿」出席，不影响成绩。

words.enDefinition: approximately, used after a number

examples.en: The walk from the dorm to class takes ten minutes or so.
examples.zh: 从宿舍走到教室需要「十分钟左右」。

examples.en: Stay for another hour or so before you head back.
examples.zh: 回去之前再待「一个来小时」吧。

words.enDefinition: have restaurant food delivered to your home

examples.en: It's raining hard tonight, so let's order in some noodles.
examples.zh: 今晚雨下得很大，我们「点外卖」吃面吧。

examples.en: We ordered in because nobody wanted to leave the dorm.
examples.zh: 因为没人想出门，我们「叫了外卖」。

collocations: order in on a rainy night

words.enDefinition: keeping plans, files, and time neatly arranged

examples.en: Nina is so organized that she color-codes every deadline in her planner.
examples.zh: 妮娜做事特别「有条理」，每个截止日期都用颜色标进计划本。

examples.en: Staying organized during finals week saves you a lot of panic.
examples.zh: 期末周保持「有条理」，能省去很多手忙脚乱。

words.enDefinition: fall asleep very quickly and deeply

examples.en: My head hit the pillow and I was out like a light.
examples.zh: 头一碰到枕头，我立刻「睡得不省人事」。

examples.en: After the eighteen-hour flight she was out like a light by nine.
examples.zh: 飞了十八个小时，她九点就「沾床睡熟了」。

collocations: out like a light by ten
hit the pillow and was out like a light

words.enDefinition: Not working and therefore unusable

examples.en: The lift was out of order, so we waited downstairs for the others.
examples.zh: 电梯「出了故障」，我们就在楼下等其他人。

examples.en: I found a note saying the hand dryer was out of order that morning.
examples.zh: 那天早上我看到一张便条，上面说烘手机「发生了故障」。

words.enDefinition: having no room left to save files or photos

examples.en: My phone is out of storage, so I cannot even download the reading PDF.
examples.zh: 我手机「存储空间不足」，连阅读PDF都下载不了。

examples.en: The camera refused to record because the laptop was out of storage.
examples.zh: 笔记本「存储空间不足」，相机都没法录像了。

collocations: the phone is out of storage

words.enDefinition: no longer modern or useful because things have moved on

examples.en: The department's style guide is outdated; it still wants 2005-era footnotes.
examples.zh: 系里的写作规范「过时」了，还要求 2005 年那套脚注格式。

examples.en: My outdated phone can't run the app our seminar requires.
examples.zh: 我的手机太「旧」，跑不动讨论课要求的那个应用。

words.enDefinition: a set of clothes worn together for an occasion

examples.en: I picked a comfortable outfit for the long day of lectures.
examples.zh: 要上一整天课，我挑了「一身舒服的衣服」。

examples.en: She laid out her outfit for the presentation the night before.
examples.zh: 她前一晚就摆好了第二天演讲的「一身衣服」。

collocations: plan my outfit the night before

words.enDefinition: friendly and energetic, comfortable around new people

examples.en: My outgoing roommate organized a floor dinner during our first week.
examples.zh: 我那位「外向的」室友在开学第一周就组织了楼层聚餐。

examples.en: Outgoing people often become the glue of a student club.
examples.zh: 「外向的人」常常是一个社团的黏合剂。

words.enDefinition: a thick glove for handling hot dishes from the oven

examples.en: Use the oven mitt when you pull the hot dish out.
examples.zh: 把热菜端出来时要戴上「隔热手套」。

examples.en: There's only one oven mitt left in our shared dorm kitchen.
examples.zh: 宿舍公共厨房里只剩一只「烤箱手套」了。

words.enDefinition: the same thing repeated many times

examples.en: I played the lecture recording over and over to catch every term.
examples.zh: 我「一遍又一遍」地放讲座录音，想听清每个术语。

examples.en: She practiced her presentation over and over in front of the mirror.
examples.zh: 她对着镜子「一遍又一遍」地练习展示。

words.enDefinition: extremely happy and pleased about something, informal

examples.en: She was over the moon when she won the essay competition.
examples.zh: 作文比赛获奖时，她「欣喜若狂」。

examples.en: Mom was over the moon when I told her I passed my exams.
examples.zh: 我告诉妈妈考试都通过时，她「乐开了花」。

words.enDefinition: covered with a full layer of gray clouds

examples.en: The sky stayed overcast, and our beach trip felt gloomy.
examples.zh: 天空一直是「阴沉沉的」，我们的海边之行都显得无精打采。

examples.en: Overcast mornings actually make the photo studio perfect for portraits.
examples.zh: 「阴天」的早晨其实最适合在摄影棚拍人像。

words.enDefinition: to eat more food than your body needs

examples.en: I always overeat at buffets because everything looks so good.
examples.zh: 自助餐什么都好吃，我每次都「吃得过多」。

examples.en: Try not to overeat late at night; it ruins your sleep.
examples.zh: 深夜别「吃太多」，会影响睡眠。

words.enDefinition: flow over the edges because there is too much

examples.en: Leave the sink running and it will overflow onto the floor.
examples.zh: 水池的水龙头不关，水会「溢出」流到地板上。

examples.en: The trash can overflowed because pickup was delayed by the holiday.
examples.zh: 垃圾清运因假期推迟，垃圾桶都「满得溢出来」了。

words.enDefinition: Extra seating for people the main area cannot hold

examples.en: The volunteer directed us to overflow seating when the main room filled up.
examples.zh: 主厅坐满后，志愿者领我们去了「客满时加设的座位」那里。

examples.en: The event had overflow seating in another room with a view of the stage.
examples.zh: 活动在另一间能看到舞台的房间里设了「客满时加设的座位」。

words.enDefinition: A spoken message played over a loudspeaker system

examples.en: The overhead announcement said the afternoon group should move to the other entrance.
examples.zh: 「公共广播」说下午场那一组应该换到另一个入口。

examples.en: We heard an overhead announcement just as the doors to the hall opened.
examples.zh: 大厅门刚一打开，我们就听到了一段「公共广播」。

words.enDefinition: become dangerously hot after long use or charging

examples.en: My laptop overheats whenever I run the design software with twenty browser tabs.
examples.zh: 开着设计软件再挂二十个网页，我的笔记本就会「发烫」。

examples.en: Your phone overheats fast under a blanket, so leave it on the desk while charging.
examples.zh: 手机在被窝里很容易「发烫」，充电时还是放在桌上吧。

words.enDefinition: priced too high for what you get

examples.en: That campus bookstore is overpriced; order your books online instead.
examples.zh: 校园书店「定价太高」，教材还是网上下单吧。

examples.en: The coffee is decent but the pastries are honestly overpriced.
examples.zh: 咖啡还行，可那些糕点真是「贵得离谱」。

words.enDefinition: not as good as many people claim

examples.en: Honestly, that cafe near campus is overrated—the coffee is just average.
examples.zh: 说实话，学校附近那家咖啡店「被高估」了，咖啡就是普通水平。

examples.en: Some classmates call that major overrated, but I still find its courses useful.
examples.zh: 有些同学说这个专业「名过其实」，但我还是觉得课程挺有用。

words.enDefinition: a heavy shirt worn over another top like a jacket

examples.en: I wore an overshirt over my T-shirt because the lecture hall is usually cool.
examples.zh: 阶梯教室通常有点凉，我就在T恤外加了件「外搭衬衫」。

examples.en: The overshirt was easy to take off when our group moved into the warm studio.
examples.zh: 我们小组进了暖和的工作室后，那件「外搭衬衫」很容易脱下来。

words.enDefinition: accidentally sleep longer than you intended

examples.en: I overslept and missed the free shuttle to the airport.
examples.zh: 我「睡过头」了，错过了去机场的免费班车。

examples.en: Set two alarms in winter—it's easy to oversleep in a warm room.
examples.zh: 冬天设两个闹钟吧，屋里一暖就容易「睡过头」。

words.enDefinition: feeling unable to deal with everything at once

examples.en: With five deadlines next week, I'm honestly feeling a bit overwhelmed.
examples.zh: 下周有五个截止日期，说实话我有点「不堪重负」。

examples.en: Many new international students feel overwhelmed by the English paperwork.
examples.zh: 很多新留学生都被英文材料手续搞得「手足无措」。

words.enDefinition: very great in amount or effect and hard to handle

examples.en: The first week's reading list felt overwhelming, so my study group split the chapters.
examples.zh: 第一周的阅读清单「多得吓人」，我们学习小组就分章认领了。

examples.en: The international office gave us overwhelming support—campus tours, SIM cards, even a welcome lunch.
examples.zh: 国际学生办公室的支持「铺天盖地」：校园导览、电话卡，还有欢迎午餐。

words.enDefinition: to prepare food at home to eat later at school

examples.en: I pack a lunch every night to avoid the dining hall lines.
examples.zh: 我每晚都「带饭」，免得在食堂排长队。

examples.en: Packing a lunch saves me at least fifty dollars a month.
examples.zh: 「自带午饭」每月至少帮我省五十美元。

collocations: pack a lunch the night before
save money by packing a lunch

words.enDefinition: put your things into bags before leaving

examples.en: We packed up the picnic things as soon as the drizzle started.
examples.zh: 毛毛雨一下起来，我们就把野餐的东西「打包」了。

examples.en: It's almost closing time, so start packing up your laptop and notes.
examples.zh: 快到闭馆时间了，开始把电脑和笔记「收」起来吧。

words.enDefinition: completely full of people with no space left

examples.en: The gym gets packed right after five, so I go before my first class.
examples.zh: 健身房五点后「人满为患」，所以我第一节课前先去。

examples.en: The dining hall was so packed that we ate standing by the window.
examples.zh: 食堂「挤」得水泄不通，我们只能靠窗站着吃。

words.enDefinition: causing no pain, trouble, or difficulty

examples.en: The online tax form was surprisingly painless once I gathered all my documents.
examples.zh: 备齐材料后，线上报税表填起来出乎意料地「轻松省事」。
