examples.en: I had to restack the papers after they slid off the desk.
examples.zh: 纸张从书桌上滑下去后，我只好「重新叠放」。

examples.en: My classmate helped me restack the trays beside the café counter.
examples.zh: 同学帮我把托盘在咖啡馆柜台旁「重新叠放」好。

words.enDefinition: turn a device off and on again to fix it

examples.en: Restart the router first; that quick fix solves most dorm Wi-Fi problems.
examples.zh: 先「重启」路由器，这个小操作能解决宿舍Wi-Fi的大部分问题。

examples.en: The technician told me to restart my laptop before calling again.
examples.zh: 技术员让我先「重启」笔记本，然后再打电话。

words.enDefinition: unable to relax or stay still, often from worry or boredom

examples.en: I felt restless all evening, pacing around my dorm room.
examples.zh: 整个晚上我都「静不下来」，在宿舍里走来走去。

examples.en: The day before results come out, everyone gets restless in class.
examples.zh: 出成绩的前一天，课堂上大家都「坐立不安」。

words.enDefinition: go back along the exact path you took before

examples.en: Retrace your steps from the dining hall; your card was last used there.
examples.zh: 从食堂开始「循原路返回」找，你的校园卡最后一次是在那儿用的。

examples.en: I retraced my steps through the library twice before giving up.
examples.zh: 我在图书馆来回「原路找」了两遍才放弃。

words.enDefinition: able to be used again instead of thrown away

examples.en: Bring a reusable cup and the campus cafe knocks ten percent off.
examples.zh: 自带「可重复使用」的杯子，校园咖啡馆还打九折。

examples.en: I pack reusable shopping bags so I never buy plastic at the store.
examples.zh: 我总在包里放几个「环保」购物袋，就省得在店里买塑料袋。

words.enDefinition: designed to be worn with either side facing outwards

examples.en: I wore the plain side of my reversible jacket to dinner with my project group.
examples.zh: 跟项目组一起吃晚饭时，我把「两面可穿的」夹克翻到素色那面穿。

examples.en: The reversible vest let us switch team colors halfway through practice on the field.
examples.zh: 「两面可穿的」背心让我们能在球场训练到一半时换队服颜色。

words.enDefinition: A door with panels rotating around a central point

examples.en: I had never used a revolving door with a bag this big before.
examples.zh: 我以前没拎着这么大的包走过「旋转门」。

examples.en: The revolving door led into the lobby where my flatmate was already waiting.
examples.zh: 「旋转门」通向门厅，室友已经在那里等我。

words.enDefinition: giving something valuable for the effort you put in

examples.en: Volunteering at the writing center is slow going but deeply rewarding.
examples.zh: 在写作中心做志愿进展缓慢，却让我「收获满满」。

examples.en: The research internship was rewarding once I finally understood the data.
examples.zh: 等我终于看懂数据，这段科研实习就「很值」了。

words.enDefinition: to move playback backward so an earlier part can be played again

examples.en: Could you rewind a little so I can hear what the speaker said?
examples.zh: 你能「把播放进度往回倒」一点吗？我想听清讲者说了什么。

examples.en: I tried to rewind the recording to find the instructions for the assignment.
examples.zh: 我试着「把播放进度往回倒」，找作业说明。

words.enDefinition: an appliance that steams rice automatically

examples.en: A rice cooker is the first appliance every Chinese student buys here.
examples.zh: 「电饭煲」是中国留学生到这里的第一件采购。

examples.en: The rice cooker switches to keep-warm mode automatically when it finishes.
examples.zh: 「电饭煲」煮好后会自动跳到保温模式。

words.enDefinition: immediately, without waiting even a moment

examples.en: The landlord said he would fix the heating right away.
examples.zh: 房东说他会「立刻」来修暖气。

examples.en: If the smoke alarm beeps, report it to the front desk right away.
examples.zh: 烟雾报警器要是响，请「马上」报告前台。

words.enDefinition: press the secondary mouse button to open extra options

examples.en: Right-click the file and choose rename before uploading the assignment.
examples.zh: 上传作业之前，「右键点击」文件并选择重命名。

examples.en: On the lab computers you cannot right-click the desktop, so use the menu bar.
examples.zh: 机房的电脑不能对桌面「右键点击」，只能用菜单栏。

words.enDefinition: fixed and strict, unwilling to bend or change

examples.en: The professor was rigid about deadlines until a student explained her visa-related delays.
examples.zh: 教授对截止日期一向「死板」，直到有学生解释了签证带来的延误。

examples.en: Our rigid chore schedule fell apart during finals, so we switched to a shared app.
examples.zh: 期末周「僵化」的值日表垮了，我们换成了共享应用。

words.enDefinition: the sound a phone makes when someone calls you

examples.en: My ringtone is still the default one because I never figured out how to change it.
examples.zh: 我的「手机铃声」还是默认的，因为一直没搞明白怎么换。

examples.en: His ringtone goes off in the library at the worst possible moment.
examples.zh: 他的「手机铃声」总在图书馆里最不该响的时候响起来。

words.enDefinition: wash something quickly with clean water

examples.en: Please rinse the plates before you load them into the dishwasher.
examples.zh: 放洗碗机之前，请先把盘子「冲洗」一下。

examples.en: I rinsed the spinach three times to get rid of the sand.
examples.zh: 我把菠菜「冲洗」了三遍，去掉里面的沙子。

words.enDefinition: remove something from hair or fabric by washing it away with water

examples.en: I stayed in the shower a bit longer to rinse out the rest of the shampoo.
examples.zh: 我在淋浴间多待了一会儿，把剩余的洗发水「冲洗掉」。

examples.en: I had to rinse out the conditioner before turning off the water in the shower.
examples.zh: 关淋浴的水之前，我得把护发素「冲洗掉」。

words.enDefinition: a cheerful way to tell someone to wake up

examples.en: Rise and shine! The dining hall stops serving breakfast in twenty minutes.
examples.zh: 「快起床」！食堂再过二十分钟就停止供应早餐了。

examples.en: My dad always said rise and shine when he came to wake me up.
examples.zh: 我爸来叫我起床的时候，总会说一句「快起床」。

collocations: wake someone with rise and shine

words.enDefinition: walk around an area freely without a fixed plan

examples.en: Roam the flea market first before you decide what to buy.
examples.zh: 跳蚤市场先「逛」一圈再决定买什么。

examples.en: Freshmen roamed the campus all week during orientation with maps.
examples.zh: 迎新那一周，新生们拿着校园地图到处「转悠」。

words.enDefinition: a person others admire and want to imitate

examples.en: My older cousin was my role model for applying to universities abroad.
examples.zh: 我的表哥是我申请出国留学的「榜样」。

examples.en: Good role models matter more to teenagers than strict rules.
examples.zh: 对青少年来说，好的「榜样」比严格的规矩更重要。

collocations: be a role model to someone
look up to a role model

words.enDefinition: flatten dough into a thin sheet with a pin

examples.en: Roll out the pizza dough on a floured counter before adding toppings.
examples.zh: 加料之前，先把披萨面团在撒了面粉的台面上「擀开」。

examples.en: She rolled out the cookie dough and cut shapes with a mug.
examples.zh: 她把饼干面团「擀开」，用马克杯当模具压出形状。

words.enDefinition: fold your sleeves upwards so they sit higher on your arms

examples.en: You might want to roll up your sleeves before washing the paintbrushes in the studio.
examples.zh: 在工作室洗画笔前，你可以先「把袖子卷起来」。

examples.en: I remember the tutor saying to roll up your sleeves before mixing the clay.
examples.zh: 我记得导师说过，和黏土前要「把袖子卷起来」。

collocations: roll up your sleeves before washing
roll up your sleeves to the elbows
remember to roll up your sleeves

words.enDefinition: move your eyes upward to show silent annoyance

examples.en: Don't roll your eyes when your roommate reminds you about rent day.
examples.zh: 室友提醒你交房租的日子时，别「翻白眼」。

examples.en: My brother rolled his eyes when Mom asked about laundry again.
examples.zh: 妈妈又问衣服洗了没，我哥「翻了个白眼」。

words.enDefinition: Enough space for one additional person

examples.en: Is there room for one more at the table beside the window over there?
examples.zh: 靠窗那张桌子「还有一个人的位置」吗？

examples.en: The people on the bench said there was room for one more near the end.
examples.zh: 长椅上的人说，靠边那儿「还有一个人的位置」。

words.enDefinition: A notice that the room is occupied

examples.en: The sign on the door said “Room in use,” so we waited outside.
examples.zh: 门上的牌子写着「房间使用中」，我们就在外面等。

examples.en: When I saw “Room in use,” I went upstairs to find an empty space.
examples.zh: 看到「房间使用中」后，我就上楼找空地方了。

collocations: mark a room as in use
a door notice reading “Room in use”

words.enDefinition: A sign identifying a room or its use

examples.en: The room sign said Craft Room, so I knew we had gone one door too far.
examples.zh: 「房间标牌」上写着手工室，我才知道我们多走过了一扇门。

examples.en: I took a picture of the room sign so my classmate could find us.
examples.zh: 我拍下「房间标牌」，方便同学找到我们。

collocations: a room sign on the door

words.enDefinition: a person who shares your room or apartment

examples.en: My roommate and I split the groceries and cleaning duties evenly.
examples.zh: 我和「室友」平分买菜和打扫的任务。

examples.en: My roommate is a night owl, so I bought an eye mask.
examples.zh: 我的「室友」是个夜猫子，所以我买了个眼罩。

words.enDefinition: an unverified story passed from person to person

examples.en: The rumor about a surprise quiz spread through the group chat in minutes.
examples.zh: 关于突击测验的「谣言」几分钟就在群里传开了。

examples.en: Don't believe every rumor you hear in the dorm hallway.
examples.zh: 别相信宿舍走廊里听到的每一条「传闻」。

words.enDefinition: do small practical jobs around town

examples.en: I'm running errands downtown this afternoon, so do you need anything?
examples.zh: 今天下午我要去市区「办点杂事」，你需要带什么吗？

examples.en: She spent the whole morning running errands around the campus area.
examples.zh: 她一上午都在学校周边「跑腿办事」。

words.enDefinition: meet someone unexpectedly by chance

examples.en: I ran into my cousin at the grocery store downtown.
examples.zh: 我在市区的超市「偶遇」了表哥。

examples.en: You'll never guess who I ran into on campus today.
examples.zh: 你绝对猜不到我今天在校园里「碰见」了谁。

words.enDefinition: to be behind time and likely to arrive late

examples.en: Sorry, I am running late because the bus broke down.
examples.zh: 抱歉，我「快迟到了」，公交车半路抛锚了。

examples.en: The meeting ran late, so I had to skip my tutorial.
examples.zh: 会议开「超时」了，我只好翘掉辅导课。

words.enDefinition: to have very little of something left

examples.en: We're running low on laundry detergent, add it to the shopping list.
examples.zh: 我们的洗衣液「快用完了」，把它加进购物清单吧。

examples.en: My meal plan funds are running low before the end of term.
examples.zh: 学期结束前，我的餐费余额就「快用完了」。

words.enDefinition: have no more of something left to use

examples.en: We ran out of coffee filters, so can you buy some?
examples.zh: 咖啡滤纸「用完」了，你能买些吗？

examples.en: The printer ran out of ink in the middle of my essay.
examples.zh: 打印机在我打印论文时「没墨了」。

words.enDefinition: to use up all the available time

examples.en: I ran out of time on the multiple-choice section again.
examples.zh: 选择题部分我又「没来得及做完」。

examples.en: We ran out of time before covering the last chapter.
examples.zh: 最后一章还没讲到，时间就「不够用」了。

collocations: run out of time in an exam

words.enDefinition: old and in poor condition from neglect

examples.en: The building looks rundown outside, but the flat inside is actually fine.
examples.zh: 楼从外面看挺「破旧」，里面的公寓倒还行。

examples.en: They raised the rent on a rundown place with the same broken elevator.
examples.zh: 电梯坏着不修，这么「破」的房子居然还涨租。

words.enDefinition: leave home very fast because you are late

examples.en: I rushed out the door without breakfast and bought a bagel on campus.
examples.zh: 我「冲出家门」，早餐都没吃，到学校才买了贝果。

examples.en: Don't rush out the door; double-check that you have your student ID.
examples.zh: 别急着「冲出门」，再检查一下学生证带没带。

collocations: rushed out the door without breakfast
about to rush out the door

words.enDefinition: open shoes held on the foot by straps

examples.en: I wore sandals to the outdoor film because the evening was still warm.
examples.zh: 晚上依旧暖和，所以我穿着「凉鞋」去看露天电影。

examples.en: My sandals fit easily into the side of my bag beside my towel.
examples.zh: 我的「凉鞋」很容易塞进包的一侧，放在毛巾旁边。

words.enDefinition: making you feel pleased and content

examples.en: There's something deeply satisfying about folding warm laundry straight from the dryer.
examples.zh: 把刚烘干的衣服叠好，有种说不出的「畅快」。

examples.en: Crossing the finish line of my first 10K was the most satisfying moment this year.
examples.zh: 完成人生第一个十公里的冲线时刻，是今年最「令人畅快」的一刻。

words.enDefinition: store your work so it is kept after closing

examples.en: Save your essay to two places while you write, not just the desktop.
examples.zh: 写论文时就要把文章「保存」到两个地方，别只存桌面。

examples.en: The browser crashed before I could save my paragraph, and I lost ten minutes.
examples.zh: 浏览器崩了没来得及「保存」我的段落，十分钟白写了。

words.enDefinition: keep money gradually for a future purchase

examples.en: I'm saving up for a new laptop before term starts.
examples.zh: 开学前我正在为换新笔记本电脑「攒钱」。

examples.en: She saved up for two months to buy the bicycle.
examples.zh: 她「攒了」两个月的钱才买下那辆自行车。

collocations: save up for a new phone

words.enDefinition: make a digital copy with a machine or phone camera

examples.en: Scan the QR code at the library entrance instead of showing your card.
examples.zh: 在图书馆入口「扫」二维码就行，不用出示学生卡。

examples.en: I scanned my passport and emailed the copy to the housing office.
examples.zh: 我把护照「扫描」了一份，用邮件发给了住房办公室。

words.enDefinition: not easy to find because there is little

examples.en: Study rooms are scarce during finals week, so book ahead.
examples.zh: 期末周自习室很「紧缺」，所以要提前预订。

examples.en: Cheap apartments near campus are scarce this time of year.
examples.zh: 每年这个时候，校园附近的便宜公寓都很「稀缺」。

words.enDefinition: angrily criticize someone, often a child

examples.en: Mom scolded me for skipping family dinner to watch the game.
examples.zh: 我为了看球赛没吃家宴，被妈妈「训斥」了一顿。

examples.en: The landlady scolded us for microwaving fish in the shared kitchen.
examples.zh: 房东太太因为我们在公共厨房热鱼而「责骂」了我们。

words.enDefinition: lift food or liquid out with a rounded tool

examples.en: Scoop the rice into the bowl before it gets sticky and cold.
examples.zh: 趁米饭还没变黏变凉，赶紧「舀」进碗里。

examples.en: He scooped ice cream for everyone after the long study session.
examples.zh: 一起自习结束后，他给大家「舀」了冰淇淋。

words.enDefinition: burning hot, like the midday summer sun

examples.en: The scorching sidewalk made my walk to class truly miserable.
examples.zh: 「灼热」的人行道让我上学的路格外难受。

examples.en: We moved the picnic table into the shade during the scorching afternoon.
examples.zh: 「烈日炎炎」的下午，我们把野餐桌挪到了阴凉处。

words.enDefinition: climb quickly using both hands and feet

examples.en: We scrambled up the rocky trail to catch sunrise at the lookout.
examples.zh: 为了在观景台看日出，我们「手脚并用地爬」上了乱石坡。

examples.en: I scrambled up the bunk ladder when my alarm finally went off.
examples.zh: 闹钟终于响时，我「手脚并用」爬上了上铺。

words.enDefinition: marked with thin surface lines or scrapes

examples.en: The secondhand laptop was cheap because the lid is badly scratched.
examples.zh: 这台二手笔记本便宜，就因为顶盖「划痕」很重。

examples.en: Our landlord charged us for a scratched door that was already like that.
examples.zh: 那扇门本来就是「花」的，房东还照样收我们钱。

words.enDefinition: a thin clear film that guards a phone screen from scratches

examples.en: I just put a new screen protector on my phone after cracking the last one.
examples.zh: 上一个贴膜碎掉之后，我刚给手机换了张新的「屏幕保护膜」。

examples.en: The screen protector saved my screen when my phone fell off the desk.
examples.zh: 手机从桌上摔下去时，「屏幕保护膜」救了屏幕一命。

words.enDefinition: the amount of time spent looking at devices each day

examples.en: My weekly screen time report said nine hours a day, which was humbling.
examples.zh: 每周「屏幕使用时间」报告显示我每天玩九小时，有点扎心。

examples.en: I set app limits in screen time settings to use my phone less.
examples.zh: 我在「屏幕使用时间」设置里给应用加了限额，好少玩手机。

words.enDefinition: move content up or down on a screen

examples.en: I scrolled through the group chat to find the room booking link.
examples.zh: 我在群聊里来回「翻找」，想找到订房链接。

examples.en: Scroll down to the bottom of the page and click agree.
examples.zh: 把页面往下「滑动」到底，然后点击同意。

words.enDefinition: rub something hard with a brush to clean it

examples.en: I scrubbed the burnt pot for half an hour after Sunday dinner.
examples.zh: 周日晚饭后，我把糊了的锅「刷洗」了半个小时。

examples.en: You'll need to scrub the shower tiles; wiping won't remove that mold.
examples.zh: 淋浴间的瓷砖得用力「刷」，擦是擦不掉那些霉斑的。

words.enDefinition: untidy and uncared for in appearance

examples.en: He looked scruffy after finals week—three-day stubble and a wrinkled hoodie.
examples.zh: 期末周过后他「邋里邋遢」，三天没刮的胡子和皱卫衣。

examples.en: The scruffy puppy at the shelter turned out to be the friendliest one there.
examples.zh: 收容所里那只「邋遢」的小狗其实是最亲人的。

words.enDefinition: move quickly with small, hurried steps

examples.en: Students scurry between the two buildings when the ten-minute break starts.
examples.zh: 十分钟课间一开始，学生们就在两座教学楼之间「小跑着」穿梭。

examples.en: Mice scurried along the wall of the old basement storage.
examples.zh: 老地下室储物间的墙边有老鼠「窜来窜去」。

words.enDefinition: a line where two pieces of fabric are joined

examples.en: I found a loose thread along the side seam of my jacket after rehearsal.
examples.zh: 排练过后，我发现夹克侧面的「接缝」上有个松了的线头。

examples.en: The seam on the inside of my sleeve caught on the corner of the shelf.
examples.zh: 袖子里面的「接缝」被架子的尖角勾住了。

words.enDefinition: the box where you type words to search within a site or app

examples.en: Just type the course code into the search bar and it will pop up.
examples.zh: 把课程代码输进「搜索框」，课程信息就会弹出来。

examples.en: The search bar at the top of the app finds any building on campus.
examples.zh: 应用顶部的「搜索框」能找到校园里的任何一栋楼。

words.enDefinition: a website that finds pages matching the words you type

examples.en: I use a different search engine for school research because it shows academic sources first.
examples.zh: 做学术研究我用另一个「搜索引擎」，它会优先显示学术来源。

examples.en: Type the exact error message into the search engine and a fix usually appears.
examples.zh: 把报错信息原样输进「搜索引擎」，通常就能找到解决办法。

words.enDefinition: A space set aside for people to sit

examples.en: We waited in the seating area by the doors while the room was being opened.
examples.zh: 房间还没开门时，我们在门旁的「座位区」等着。

examples.en: The seating area outside the hall was quieter than the one near the entrance.
examples.zh: 大厅外的「座位区」比入口旁的那个安静。

words.enDefinition: The total number of seats available in a space

examples.en: I asked about the seating capacity before booking the hall for our reading group.
examples.zh: 给读书小组预约大厅前，我问了「可容纳的座位数」。

examples.en: The room guide listed the seating capacity for each arrangement of tables and chairs.
examples.zh: 房间指南按桌椅的不同摆法列出了各自「可容纳的座位数」。

words.enDefinition: to question whether a decision or judgment you already made was right

examples.en: I started to second-guess my choice when I saw the crowded timetable.
examples.zh: 看到满满的时间表，我开始「怀疑原来的判断」。

examples.en: My friend told me not to second-guess every answer after the quiz.
examples.zh: 朋友劝我测验结束后，别再「反复怀疑」各道题的答案。

collocations: try not to second-guess a choice

words.enDefinition: another serving of food after finishing the first one

examples.en: The roast was so good that everyone asked for a second helping.
examples.zh: 烤肉太好吃了，每个人都想「再来一份」。

examples.en: I was too full for a second helping, even though grandma insisted.
examples.zh: 虽然奶奶一直劝，我已经太饱了，实在没法「再来一份」。

words.enDefinition: doubts about a decision already made or about to be made

examples.en: I had second thoughts about taking the early shift after seeing my timetable.
examples.zh: 看到课表后，我对接早班「又有些犹豫」。

examples.en: My roommate expressed second thoughts after we saw how far away the flat was.
examples.zh: 发现那套公寓离得太远后，室友说自己「又有些犹豫」。

collocations: have second thoughts about a decision

words.enDefinition: new energy that appears when you felt tired

examples.en: I got a second wind around eleven and finished the essay.
examples.zh: 十一点左右我「又来了精神」，把论文写完了。

examples.en: Cleaning got a second wind when we put on some music.
examples.zh: 放起音乐之后，我们打扫的劲头「又上来了」。

words.enDefinition: previously owned or used by someone else

examples.en: Almost all my kitchen stuff is secondhand from graduating seniors.
examples.zh: 我的厨房用品几乎都是毕业生甩卖的「二手货」。

examples.en: Buying secondhand textbooks saved me around three hundred this term.
examples.zh: 这学期买「二手」教材省了差不多三百块。

words.enDefinition: not often; rarely

examples.en: He seldom stays up late because of his morning shifts.
examples.zh: 因为要上早班，他「难得」熬夜。

examples.en: We seldom get snow this early in the semester, enjoy it.
examples.zh: 学期这么早「难得」下雪，好好享受吧。

words.enDefinition: worried about how you look or sound to other people

examples.en: I felt self-conscious speaking English in front of native speakers.
examples.zh: 在母语者面前说英语，我很「在意别人的眼光」。

examples.en: She's self-conscious about her accent, so please don't tease her.
examples.zh: 她很「在意」自己的口音，请别拿这个打趣她。

words.enDefinition: a photo you take of yourself, usually with a phone

examples.en: We took a selfie in front of the library on our first day of class.
examples.zh: 开学第一天，我们在图书馆前合拍了张「自拍」。

examples.en: The light by the window is perfect for taking a selfie.
examples.zh: 窗边的光线拍「自拍」刚刚好。

words.enDefinition: caring only about yourself and not others

examples.en: It felt selfish to keep the bigger room without asking my housemate.
examples.zh: 不问室友就占了那个大房间，我自觉很「自私」。

examples.en: Selfish roommates leave dishes for others to wash every night.
examples.zh: 「自私的」室友每晚都把碗留给别人洗。

words.enDefinition: showing good judgment and practical thinking

examples.en: My sensible roommate suggested we write a cleaning schedule instead of arguing.
examples.zh: 我那「明事理的」室友提议列一张打扫值日表，而不是争吵。

examples.en: A sensible choice is texting your host family before you arrive late.
examples.zh: 「明智」的做法是，会晚到就提前告诉寄宿家庭。

words.enDefinition: easily hurt by criticism or upset by small things

examples.en: She is sensitive about her accent, so avoid joking about it.
examples.zh: 她对自己的口音很「敏感」，别拿这个开玩笑。

examples.en: My sensitive little brother cried at the end of every cartoon.
examples.zh: 我「敏感的」弟弟看动画片结尾都会哭。

words.enDefinition: the amount of food one package considers a portion

examples.en: Check the serving size before assuming the whole bag is one portion.
examples.zh: 先看「每份含量」，别以为一整袋就是一份。

examples.en: The serving size listed on this ramen pack is only half the package.
examples.zh: 这个泡面标注的「每份含量」居然只有半包。

collocations: the serving size on the label

words.enDefinition: save a note that alerts you at a chosen time

examples.en: Set a reminder for the rent deadline so you never pay it late.
examples.zh: 给交房租的截止日期「设置提醒」，就再也不会迟交了。

examples.en: I set a reminder to call my grandma every Sunday evening.
examples.zh: 我给每周日晚上给奶奶打电话这件事「设置提醒」。

words.enDefinition: choose a time for your phone or clock to wake you

examples.en: I set an alarm for 6:30 so I have time to eat breakfast.
examples.zh: 我「设了六点半的闹钟」，好留时间吃早餐。

examples.en: Before an early morning exam, always set an alarm on your phone too.
examples.zh: 早上要早起考试的话，记得在手机上「多设一个闹钟」。

collocations: set two alarms just in case

words.enDefinition: begin a journey from your starting point

examples.en: We set off early to avoid the holiday traffic jams.
examples.zh: 为了避开假日的堵车，我们一大早就「动身」了。

examples.en: They set off for the coast right after sunrise on Saturday.
examples.zh: 周六日出刚过他们就「出发」去海边了。

collocations: set off early in the morning
set off on a road trip

words.enDefinition: place dishes and cutlery ready for a meal

examples.en: You set the table and I'll bring the food out.
examples.zh: 你来「摆好餐具」，我把菜端出来。

examples.en: Our host asked us to help set the table for dinner.
examples.zh: 房东让我们帮忙为晚餐「摆好餐具」。

words.enDefinition: prepare a device or place so it is ready to use

examples.en: It took an hour to set up the new printer upstairs.
examples.zh: 「装好」楼上的新打印机花了一个小时。

examples.en: We set up the projector in the common room for movie night.
examples.zh: 电影之夜我们在公共活动室「布置好」了投影仪。

words.enDefinition: the menu where you adjust how a device or app works

examples.en: Go into settings and turn off those annoying notification sounds.
examples.zh: 进「设置」把那些烦人的提示音关掉。

examples.en: I changed my language settings to English to practice every day.
examples.zh: 我把语言「设置」改成了英文，好每天练习。

words.enDefinition: more than two but not very many

examples.en: I've already asked several classmates about the assignment deadline today.
examples.zh: 今天我已经问过「几个」同学作业的截止时间了。

examples.en: The campus bus stops at several places near the dorms.
examples.zh: 校园班车在宿舍附近的「几个」地方停靠。

words.enDefinition: worn out and looking poor in condition

examples.en: The once-shabby guesthouse was renovated last year and now hosts exchange students.
examples.zh: 那家曾经「破旧」的小旅馆去年翻新，现在接待交换生。

examples.en: He keeps his shabby old sneakers for the gym even after buying new ones.
examples.zh: 买了新鞋之后，他还是穿着那双「破旧」的旧鞋去健身房。

words.enDefinition: grasp another person's hand in greeting or agreement

examples.en: Shake hands firmly with each interviewer at the career fair.
examples.zh: 招聘会上和每位面试官「握手」要有力。

examples.en: The two roommates shook hands and agreed on the cleaning rota.
examples.zh: 两个室友「握了握手」，约定好了卫生轮值表。

words.enDefinition: shake a cloth or object to remove folds, dust, or water

examples.en: Shake out the beach towel before folding it back up.
examples.zh: 收沙滩巾之前先「抖一抖」再叠。

examples.en: She shook out her wet umbrella in the stairwell, not in class.
examples.zh: 她在楼道里「抖」了抖湿雨伞，没带进教室。

words.enDefinition: moving or feeling unsteady from side to side

examples.en: The table in the back corner is shaky, so our coffee keeps spilling.
examples.zh: 后面角落那张桌子「晃」，咖啡一直往外洒。

examples.en: My voice felt shaky during the first minute of the presentation.
examples.zh: 课堂展示的第一分钟，我的声音都在「发颤」。

words.enDefinition: deserving blame and a feeling of shame

examples.en: Dropping litter right beside the recycling bins is honestly shameful behavior.
examples.zh: 就在回收桶旁边乱扔垃圾，这种行为说真的挺「可耻」。

examples.en: It's shameful when group members take credit for slides they never even opened.
examples.zh: 组员抢走自己连开都没开过的幻灯片的功劳，实在「可耻」。

words.enDefinition: A table used by several people or groups

examples.en: I found space at a shared table and opened my notebook beside another student.
examples.zh: 我在「共用桌」上找到空位，在另一位学生旁边打开笔记本。

examples.en: We left one end of the shared table clear for people who arrived later.
examples.zh: 我们把「共用桌」的一头空出来，留给后面来的人。

words.enDefinition: having a fine edge that cuts easily

examples.en: Bring a sharp knife to cooking club; dull ones slip and cause cuts.
examples.zh: 烹饪社要带「锋利」的刀，钝刀反而容易打滑伤手。

examples.en: There's a sharp edge on the broken shelf, so tape it over.
examples.zh: 坏掉的架子边缘很「利」，先用胶带缠一下。

words.enDefinition: a soft product applied to the skin before shaving

examples.en: I took a tube of shaving cream down the hall to the shared bathroom.
examples.zh: 我拿着一管「剃须膏」穿过走廊，去了共用浴室。

examples.en: The shaving cream was in my wash bag beside the toothbrush and comb.
examples.zh: 「剃须膏」在我的洗漱包里，放在牙刷和梳子旁边。

words.enDefinition: shake a little because your body feels cold

examples.en: We shivered through the entire outdoor orientation in late January.
examples.zh: 一月末的户外迎新活动，我们全程「冻得直哆嗦」。

examples.en: I shivered in the library until I found the seat by the radiator.
examples.zh: 图书馆里我「冻得发抖」，直到找到暖气片旁的座位。

words.enDefinition: very surprised by something bad or unexpected

examples.en: I was shocked to see my electricity bill this month.
examples.zh: 看到这个月的电费账单，我「惊呆」了。

examples.en: Everyone was shocked when the quiet guy won the talent show.
examples.zh: 那个安静的男生赢了才艺比赛，大家都「震惊」了。

words.enDefinition: the bottom part of a shoe that touches the ground

examples.en: A pebble got wedged in my shoe sole during our walk along the river.
examples.zh: 我们沿河散步时，一颗小石子卡在了我的「鞋底」上。

examples.en: I noticed mud on my shoe sole before stepping into the study room.
examples.zh: 走进自习室前，我发现「鞋底」上有泥。

words.enDefinition: a cord threaded through a shoe to fasten it

examples.en: I tucked a loose shoelace into my shoe before going down the dorm stairs.
examples.zh: 下宿舍楼梯前，我把一根松掉的「鞋带」塞进鞋里。

examples.en: One shoelace broke just as I was getting ready to leave for class.
examples.zh: 我刚准备出门上课，一根「鞋带」就断了。

words.enDefinition: compare prices at different stores before buying

examples.en: Shop around online before you buy the flight ticket home.
examples.zh: 买回家的机票前先在网上「货比三家」。

examples.en: We shopped around and found a much cheaper phone plan.
examples.zh: 我们「多比了几家」，找到了便宜得多的手机套餐。

collocations: shop around for the best price

words.enDefinition: getting angry quickly and easily

examples.en: Dad gets short-tempered whenever he drives in heavy city traffic.
examples.zh: 爸爸在市区堵车时特别「容易发火」。

examples.en: My short-tempered lab partner apologized right after snapping at us.
examples.zh: 我那位「容易发火的」实验搭档冲我们发完火，马上就道歉了。

words.enDefinition: a situation where not enough of something exists

examples.en: There's a shortage of parking spots near the science building.
examples.zh: 理科教学楼附近「停车位短缺」。

examples.en: The cafe hired extra staff because of a shortage of workers.
examples.zh: 因为「人手短缺」，咖啡店多招了几名员工。

words.enDefinition: push someone or something roughly and with force

examples.en: The crowd outside the concert started to shove, so I stepped aside.
examples.zh: 演唱会门外的人群开始「猛推」，我只好闪到一边。

examples.en: Don't shove your laundry bag into the closet; it will fall right back out.
examples.zh: 别把洗衣袋「猛塞」进衣柜，它马上会掉出来。

words.enDefinition: guide a visitor to see a new place

examples.en: Let me show you around the neighborhood this weekend if you're free.
examples.zh: 这周末你要是有空，我带你「逛逛」附近。

examples.en: She showed the visiting students around the main campus this morning.
examples.zh: 今天上午她带来访的学生「参观」了主校园。

words.enDefinition: arrive at a place or event as expected

examples.en: Only four people showed up to the first floor meeting of the term.
examples.zh: 本学期第一次楼层会议只有四个人「到场」。

examples.en: He showed up twenty minutes late with a coffee in each hand.
examples.zh: 他两手各拿一杯咖啡才「露面」，迟到了二十分钟。

words.enDefinition: a container for carrying or holding things used in the shower

examples.en: I carry my shower caddy down the hall when I use the shared bathroom.
examples.zh: 用共用浴室时，我会提着「淋浴用品篮」走过走廊。

examples.en: The shower caddy fits under my desk when I'm not using the shared showers.
examples.zh: 不用共用淋浴间时，「淋浴用品篮」正好可以收在我书桌下面。

words.enDefinition: a waterproof cap that keeps hair dry in the shower

examples.en: I wore a shower cap because I had already washed my hair after practice.
examples.zh: 我训练后已经洗过头，所以洗澡时戴了「浴帽」。

examples.en: She hung the shower cap beside her towel before heading back to her room.
examples.zh: 回房间前，她把「浴帽」挂在毛巾旁边。

words.enDefinition: become smaller in size after being washed or dried

examples.en: My favorite sweater shrank two sizes in the hot dryer.
examples.zh: 我最喜欢的毛衣在热烘干机里「缩了」两码。

examples.en: Wash cotton in cold water so it doesn't shrink in the machine.
examples.zh: 棉质的要用冷水洗，免得在机器里「缩水」。

collocations: washed it hot and it shrank

words.enDefinition: walk slowly without lifting your feet off the ground

examples.en: He shuffled to the bathroom half asleep before his 7:30 shift.
examples.zh: 七点半要上班，他睡眼惺忪地「拖着脚」挪去洗漱。

examples.en: We shuffled along in the slow lunch line, half awake.
examples.zh: 排午饭长队时大家睡意未消，一步步「磨蹭着」往前挪。

words.enDefinition: close everything and turn a computer off

examples.en: Shut down your laptop properly; closing the lid isn't the same.
examples.zh: 要正确「关机」，直接合上盖子可不算。

examples.en: The lab computers shut down automatically at ten every night.
examples.zh: 机房电脑每晚十点「自动关机」。

words.enDefinition: nervous and quiet when meeting new people

examples.en: I was too shy to introduce myself on the first day of class.
examples.zh: 开学第一天，我「害羞」得不敢自我介绍。

examples.en: My shy deskmate opened up once we started studying together.
examples.zh: 一起自习之后，我那位「腼腆的」同桌慢慢放开了。

words.enDefinition: a brother or sister who shares your parents

examples.en: Being an only child, I always wished I had a sibling to play with.
examples.zh: 作为独生子女，我一直希望有个「兄弟姐妹」陪自己玩。

examples.en: Sibling rivalry got intense whenever my brother borrowed my laptop.
examples.zh: 弟弟一借走我的电脑，我们「手足之间」就免不了一番较量。

words.enDefinition: An entrance on the side of a building

examples.en: The side entrance was closer to the room where our reading group met.
examples.zh: 「侧门」离读书小组碰面的房间更近。

examples.en: A sign asked visitors to use the side entrance while the front steps were blocked.
examples.zh: 正门台阶无法通行，告示请访客从「侧门」进出。

words.enDefinition: a line dividing the hair to one side of the head

examples.en: I made a side part this morning before leaving for the campus theatre rehearsal.
examples.zh: 今天早上出门去学校剧院排练前，我给头发分了条「偏分发缝」。

examples.en: My side part shifted when I took off the hat outside the library.
examples.zh: 在图书馆外摘下帽子时，我的「偏分发缝」已经被压乱了。

collocations: wear your hair with a side part

words.enDefinition: enter your account details to start using a website

examples.en: You have to sign in with your student ID to use the library computers.
examples.zh: 用学号「登录」之后才能使用图书馆的电脑。

examples.en: The website signs me out every time, so I sign in again each morning.
examples.zh: 这个网站总是自动退出，所以我每天早上都得重新「登录」。

collocations: sign in with your student ID

words.enDefinition: exit your account so the next user cannot access it

examples.en: Always sign out of your account on shared computers in the lab.
examples.zh: 在机房的公用电脑上用完一定要「退出登录」。

examples.en: I forgot to sign out, and my friend posted a joke from my account.
examples.zh: 我忘了「退出登录」，朋友拿我的账号发了条搞笑动态。

words.enDefinition: put your name on a list to join something

examples.en: Sign up for the free gym orientation before the semester gets busy.
examples.zh: 趁学期还没忙起来，早点「报名」免费的健身房入门课。

examples.en: Have you signed up for the campus volunteering fair yet?
examples.zh: 校园志愿者招聘会你「报名」了吗？

words.enDefinition: a phone setting that stops all rings and alert sounds

examples.en: My phone was on silent mode, so I missed your call this morning.
examples.zh: 我手机开了「静音模式」，今早没接到你的电话。

examples.en: Remember to switch to silent mode before you walk into the lecture hall.
examples.zh: 走进阶梯教室之前，记得切到「静音模式」。

words.enDefinition: the knives, forks, and spoons used for eating

examples.en: The dorm kitchen drawer is always out of clean silverware.
examples.zh: 宿舍厨房抽屉里永远找不到干净的「刀叉餐具」。

examples.en: Please rinse your silverware before putting it into the dishwasher.
examples.zh: 「餐具」请先冲一下再放进洗碗机。

words.enDefinition: the small chip that connects a phone to a mobile network

examples.en: I bought a local SIM card at the airport so my phone works here.
examples.zh: 我在机场买了张本地「SIM卡」，手机在这边就能正常用了。

examples.en: My SIM card stopped working, so I have no service in my dorm.
examples.zh: 我的「SIM卡」出了问题，宿舍里完全没有信号。

words.enDefinition: alike in appearance, quality or character

examples.en: Her study method is similar to the one our tutor suggested.
examples.zh: 她的学习方法和辅导老师建议的「相似」。

examples.en: This noodle dish tastes similar to the one back home.
examples.zh: 这道面食的味道和家乡的「很像」。

words.enDefinition: drink slowly, taking very small amounts

examples.en: I sipped my latte slowly while skimming the morning news.
examples.zh: 我一边浏览早间新闻，一边「小口喝」拿铁。

examples.en: Sip water during the seminar instead of gulping it all at once.
examples.zh: 研讨课上要「小口喝水」，别一口气猛灌。

words.enDefinition: the sister of your spouse, or your sibling's wife

examples.en: My sister-in-law sent me a care package before finals week.
examples.zh: 期末周前，我的「嫂子」给我寄了一个关怀包裹。

examples.en: I practiced my English with my sister-in-law during the wedding weekend.
examples.zh: 婚礼那个周末，我和「小姑」一起练习英语。

words.enDefinition: sit on the floor with legs folded in front

examples.en: Sit cross-legged on the dorm floor if the bean bags are taken.
examples.zh: 懒人沙发被占的话，就在宿舍地板上「盘腿坐」。

examples.en: We sat cross-legged around the pizza box during the study break.
examples.zh: 学习间隙我们围着披萨盒「盘腿」坐下。

words.enDefinition: move from standing into a chair or seat

examples.en: You look tired, sit down and have some water first.
examples.zh: 你看起来很累，先「坐下」喝点水吧。

examples.en: We sat down on the bench to wait for the next bus.
examples.zh: 我们「坐」在长椅上等下一班公交。

words.enDefinition: straighten your back while sitting in a chair

examples.en: Sit up when the recruiter joins the call; first impressions count.
examples.zh: 招聘官进会议室时记得「坐直」，第一印象很重要。

examples.en: I sat up suddenly when my alarm finally rang at 7:50.
examples.zh: 闹钟 7:50 终于响时，我猛地「坐起身」。

words.enDefinition: doubting that something is true or useful

examples.en: I was skeptical about the tutoring service until my grades improved.
examples.zh: 一开始我对那家辅导机构是「怀疑」的，直到成绩真的提高。

examples.en: Professors stay skeptical of sources that have no author listed.
examples.zh: 教授们对没有署名的资料来源持「怀疑」态度。

words.enDefinition: unsafe or probably dishonest; hard to trust

examples.en: That listing with no photos and cheap rent looks totally sketchy.
examples.zh: 那个房源没照片租金还便宜，看着就特别「可疑」。

examples.en: The alley shortcut feels sketchy after dark, so I take the main road.
examples.zh: 天黑后抄小巷让人「心里发毛」，我还是走大路。

words.enDefinition: slide sideways out of control on a slippery surface

examples.en: Bikes skid on the painted crosswalk line when it rains.
examples.zh: 下雨天自行车在人行横道的标线上容易「打滑」。

examples.en: The shuttle skidded slightly on the icy road near the dorms.
examples.zh: 宿舍附近的结冰路面上，校车轻微「打滑」了一下。

words.enDefinition: to read something quickly to get the main idea or find selected information

examples.en: I had time to skim through the leaflet before my study group arrived.
examples.zh: 学习小组成员到之前，我有时间「快速浏览」宣传单。

examples.en: I stopped to skim through the instructions before picking up the form.
examples.zh: 拿表格前，我停下来「快速浏览」了一下说明。

words.enDefinition: very thin, often more than is healthy

examples.en: My cousin got skinny over summer training with his university track team.
examples.zh: 表哥随校田径队训练了一个暑假，整个人变得「精瘦」。

examples.en: He looked skinny after a semester of instant noodles, so we started cooking together.
examples.zh: 吃了一学期泡面他「瘦得脱相」，我们就开始一起做饭了。

words.enDefinition: to miss breakfast, lunch, or dinner on purpose

examples.en: I skip meals during finals week and then feel awful by evening.
examples.zh: 期末周我总是「不吃正餐」，到晚上就难受。

examples.en: Never skip a meal before a big exam; your brain needs fuel.
examples.zh: 大考前千万别「饿一顿」，大脑需要能量。

words.enDefinition: decide not to do something you normally do

examples.en: I skipped breakfast again because the dining hall line was too long.
examples.zh: 食堂队伍太长，我又「省掉」了早餐。

examples.en: Never skip the safety briefing before your first lab session.
examples.zh: 第一次进实验室之前，千万别「跳过」安全讲解。

words.enDefinition: not having had enough sleep for a long time

examples.en: Everyone in the library looks tired and sleep-deprived during finals week.
examples.zh: 期末周图书馆里的每个人看起来又累又「睡眠不足」。

examples.en: Sleep-deprived students often make careless mistakes on easy exam questions.
examples.zh: 「睡眠不足」的学生常在简单的考试题上犯低级错误。

words.enDefinition: stay in bed longer than you normally do

examples.en: I love to sleep in on Sunday mornings after a long week.
examples.zh: 忙碌一周后，我最喜欢周日早上「睡懒觉」。

examples.en: She slept in and missed breakfast with us this morning.
examples.zh: 她今天早上「睡了个懒觉」，没赶上和我们一起吃早餐。

words.enDefinition: sleep very deeply without waking at all

examples.en: I slept like a log and didn't even hear the fire drill.
examples.zh: 我「睡得很死」，连消防演习都没听见。

examples.en: After moving boxes all day, you will sleep like a log tonight.
examples.zh: 搬了一天箱子，今晚你准会「睡得特别沉」。

collocations: sleep like a log after exams
so tired I slept like a log

words.enDefinition: the fixed times you go to sleep and wake up

examples.en: My sleep schedule fell apart during the group project week.
examples.zh: 小组作业那一周，我的「作息」全乱了。

examples.en: A fixed sleep schedule matters more than sleeping eight hours once.
examples.zh: 固定的「作息时间」比偶尔睡够八小时更重要。

words.enDefinition: continue sleeping without being woken by noise

examples.en: I slept through the fire alarm and my roommate had to shake me.
examples.zh: 火警响了我都「睡着没被吵醒」，室友只好把我摇醒。

examples.en: He can sleep through construction noise right outside his window.
examples.zh: 窗外施工他都能「照睡不误」。

words.enDefinition: a night spent unable to sleep at all

examples.en: I had a sleepless night before the organic chemistry midterm.
examples.zh: 有机化学期中考试前一晚，我一夜「没合眼」。

examples.en: One more sleepless night and I'll start napping in lectures again.
examples.zh: 再来一个「不眠之夜」，我又要开始在课堂上打盹了。

collocations: a sleepless night before the exam

words.enDefinition: feeling ready to fall asleep and needing rest

examples.en: I get so sleepy in my 2 p.m. lecture that I start nodding off.
examples.zh: 下午两点的课让我特别「困」，听着听着就打起了瞌睡。

examples.en: Drink something warm if you feel sleepy while revising tonight.
examples.zh: 今晚复习时要是觉得「困」，就喝点热的提提神。

words.enDefinition: a playful name for someone who sleeps too long

examples.en: Come on, sleepyhead, the campus shuttle leaves in ten minutes!
examples.zh: 快点，「小懒虫」，校园班车十分钟后就发车了！

examples.en: My older brother is such a sleepyhead that we always miss breakfast.
examples.zh: 我哥是个「小懒虫」，我们总是赶不上早餐。

words.enDefinition: made without sleeves

examples.en: I wore a sleeveless top indoors and put a cardigan over it outside.
examples.zh: 在室内我穿「无袖的」上衣，到外面就套一件开襟毛衣。

examples.en: The costume is sleeveless, so I brought a sweater for the break between rehearsals.
examples.zh: 戏服是「无袖的」，我带了件毛衣，排练间歇可以穿。

words.enDefinition: A door that opens by moving sideways

examples.en: I saw the sliding door move to the right when the hall opened.
examples.zh: 大厅开放时，我看到「推拉门」向右移开。

examples.en: The sliding door was wide enough for two people to walk through together.
examples.zh: 这扇「推拉门」足够宽，两个人能并排走过去。

words.enDefinition: leave a place secretly and without drawing attention

examples.en: Slip away from the party early if your 8 a.m. class is brutal.
examples.zh: 早上八点的课要是很硬核，聚会就「早点悄悄离场」。

examples.en: The cat slipped away through the gap in the fence again.
examples.zh: 猫又从围栏缺口「溜走」了。

words.enDefinition: put on clothes or shoes in one easy motion

examples.en: I can slip on my shoes here before we head out to the courtyard.
examples.zh: 我们去院子之前，我可以在这儿「轻松套上」鞋。

examples.en: I'll slip on a cardigan before going downstairs to meet the rest of the group.
examples.zh: 我先「套上」一件开襟毛衣，再下楼去和其他人碰面。

collocations: slip on a pair of sandals

words.enDefinition: shoes you put on without tying laces or doing up fasteners

examples.en: I keep slip-ons by the door for quick trips to the laundry room downstairs.
examples.zh: 我在门边放了双「一脚蹬便鞋」，方便临时去楼下洗衣房。

examples.en: The slip-ons were handy when we had to leave our shoes outside the studio.
examples.zh: 我们得把鞋留在工作室外面时，「一脚蹬便鞋」穿脱起来很方便。

words.enDefinition: leave quietly without anyone noticing

examples.en: Slip out the side door if the talk runs past your shuttle time.
examples.zh: 如果讲座拖过你的校车时间，就从侧门「悄悄溜出去」。

examples.en: He slipped out of the flat before anyone saw the surprise cake.
examples.zh: 趁还没人看见惊喜蛋糕，他「溜」出了公寓。

words.enDefinition: difficult to stand or walk on safely

examples.en: Wet leaves make the quad steps dangerously slippery every autumn.
examples.zh: 每年秋天，湿树叶都会把广场台阶弄得「很滑」。

examples.en: Be careful, the tile floor near the pool is slippery.
examples.zh: 小心，泳池边的瓷砖地面「很滑」。

words.enDefinition: done carelessly and without attention to detail

examples.en: The TA marked my lab report down for sloppy units and missing labels.
examples.zh: 助教因我实验报告单位「马虎」、标签缺失而扣了分。

examples.en: His sloppy handwriting cost him real points because the grader couldn't read the proofs.
examples.zh: 他字迹「潦草」，阅卷老师看不清证明过程，实打实丢了分。

words.enDefinition: sit with your shoulders and back bent forward lazily

examples.en: Don't slouch during the online interview; sit closer to the camera.
examples.zh: 视频面试别「弓着背」坐，往镜头前靠一点。

examples.en: I slouched through the three-hour lecture until my back hurt.
examples.zh: 三小时的课我一路「含胸驼背」，下课背都疼了。

words.enDefinition: reduce your speed while moving or working

examples.en: Slow down near the school zone, the limit drops here.
examples.zh: 学校区域附近要「减速」，这里限速更低。

examples.en: I've been rushing all week, so it's time to slow down.
examples.zh: 这一整周我都赶个不停，该「放慢节奏」了。

words.enDefinition: an internet connection that loads pages and videos slowly

examples.en: Slow internet in the dorm makes uploading my lab video take an hour.
examples.zh: 宿舍「网速慢」，上传实验视频要花一个小时。

examples.en: The cafe has slow internet, but the quiet is worth it for reading.
examples.zh: 这家咖啡馆「网速慢」，但很安静，值得来读书。

collocations: the slow internet in the dorm

words.enDefinition: drop into a seat with your body bent and heavy

examples.en: She slumped into the nearest chair after the four-hour lab.
examples.zh: 四小时的实验课结束，她一进门就「瘫坐」进最近的椅子。

examples.en: I slumped over my economics notes halfway through the all-nighter.
examples.zh: 通宵刷题到一半，我「瘫」在了经济学讲义上。

words.enDefinition: light polite conversation about unimportant topics

examples.en: Elevator small talk with neighbors usually covers weather and weekend plans.
examples.zh: 电梯里和邻居的「寒暄」通常离不开天气和周末安排。

examples.en: Making small talk at orientation helped me remember fifty new names.
examples.zh: 迎新会上的「闲聊」让我和五十个新同学混了个脸熟。

words.enDefinition: neat and comfortable, in a style between casual and formal

examples.en: The student society dinner is smart casual, so I'm wearing a neat shirt and chinos.
examples.zh: 学生社团聚餐要求「穿得体面又不必太正式」，所以我穿整齐的衬衫配休闲裤。

examples.en: I asked what smart casual meant for the reception before I packed my bag.
examples.zh: 收拾行李前，我问招待会要求的「得体而不太正式」具体是怎么穿。

words.enDefinition: a wrist watch that connects to a phone and tracks activity

examples.en: My smartwatch buzzes when someone texts me during a quiet study session.
examples.zh: 安静自习时有人发消息，我的「智能手表」会轻轻震动提醒。

examples.en: He checks his sleep stats on his smartwatch every morning at breakfast.
examples.zh: 他每天吃早餐时都会在「智能手表」上看睡眠数据。

words.enDefinition: a thick blended drink of fruit, yogurt, or juice

examples.en: I make a banana smoothie before my morning gym sessions.
examples.zh: 早晨健身前我会打一杯香蕉「果昔」。

examples.en: That juice bar near campus charges eight dollars for one smoothie.
examples.zh: 校园附近那家饮品店一杯「冰沙」就要八美元。

words.enDefinition: a small amount of food eaten between meals

examples.en: I always keep a snack in my backpack for long study sessions.
examples.zh: 我包里总会放一份「零食」，长时间学习时补充体力。

examples.en: Yogurt with granola is my go-to snack during exam week.
examples.zh: 酸奶配燕麦脆是我考试周最爱的「零食」。

words.enDefinition: to eat small amounts of food between meals

examples.en: I snack on almonds while reading in the library for hours.
examples.zh: 我在图书馆一坐几个小时，期间「拿杏仁当零食」吃。

examples.en: Don't snack on chips right before dinner, or you won't be hungry.
examples.zh: 晚饭前别「拿薯片当零食」吃，不然正餐就吃不下了。

words.enDefinition: to suddenly speak angrily and sharply to someone

examples.en: Sorry I snapped at you; exam week has me exhausted.
examples.zh: 抱歉刚才「冲你发火」，考试周把我累坏了。

examples.en: She snapped at her brother for borrowing her notes again.
examples.zh: 弟弟又拿她的笔记，她「没好气地吼」了他一句。

words.enDefinition: grab something suddenly and quickly before others can react

examples.en: Snatch your umbrella before the downpour catches you between classes.
examples.zh: 趁暴雨还没在课间淋到你，赶紧「一把抓起」雨伞。

examples.en: Someone snatched my phone right off the table at the café terrace.
examples.zh: 在咖啡馆露天座，有人「一把抢走」了放在桌上的手机。

words.enDefinition: move somewhere quietly so nobody notices you

examples.en: Sneak in through the back door if you're late to the lecture.
examples.zh: 讲课迟到的话，从后门「悄悄溜进去」。

examples.en: He sneaked downstairs for midnight noodles without waking the whole flat.
examples.zh: 他半夜「蹑手蹑脚」下楼泡面，没吵醒整层公寓的人。

words.enDefinition: casual shoes with flexible soles often worn for exercise

examples.en: I wore sneakers because the campus tour involved walking between several buildings before lunch.
examples.zh: 我穿了「运动休闲鞋」，因为午饭前参观校园要在几栋楼之间走动。

examples.en: My sneakers were still damp from rain, so I left them by the door.
examples.zh: 我的「运动休闲鞋」淋了雨还没干，我把它们留在门边。

words.enDefinition: push air out suddenly and loudly through your nose

examples.en: I always sneeze when the pollen count spikes in April.
examples.zh: 四月花粉浓度一高，我就不停「打喷嚏」。

examples.en: Sneeze into your elbow, please, not toward the shared desk.
examples.zh: 请用手肘挡着「打喷嚏」，别对着公用书桌。

words.enDefinition: smell something with short breaths through the nose

examples.en: Sniff the milk first if you're not sure it's still good.
examples.zh: 拿不准牛奶有没有坏，先「闻」一下。

examples.en: He kept sniffing during the lecture because of his cold.
examples.zh: 他感冒了，整节课都在「抽鼻子」。

words.enDefinition: Cut a small part off something with scissors or a similar tool.

examples.en: Use the small scissors to snip off the loose thread before it catches on something.
examples.zh: 用小剪刀把那根松线头「剪掉」，免得挂到东西。

examples.en: I had to snip off a corner of the bag to pour out the seeds.
examples.zh: 我得「剪掉」袋角的一小截，才能把种子倒出来。

words.enDefinition: to look for private information about someone without their permission

examples.en: I told my flatmate that I would never snoop through their messages.
examples.zh: 我告诉室友，我绝不会翻他们的消息来「窥探私事」。

examples.en: The film was about a student who liked to snoop around the office.
examples.zh: 电影讲的是一个喜欢在办公室周围「窥探别人私事」的学生。

words.enDefinition: delay the alarm for a few extra minutes of sleep

examples.en: I snooze my alarm exactly three times before dragging myself to morning class.
examples.zh: 上早课前我总会按三次「贪睡」，才勉强爬起来。

examples.en: Do not snooze the alarm again, or we will miss the free breakfast.
examples.zh: 别再按「贪睡」了，不然我们就赶不上免费早餐了。

words.enDefinition: breathe noisily through the nose while sleeping

examples.en: My roommate snores so loudly that I sleep with earplugs now.
examples.zh: 我室友「打鼾」太响，我现在都戴着耳塞睡。

examples.en: He only snores when he sleeps flat on his back.
examples.zh: 他只有平躺着睡才会「打呼噜」。

words.enDefinition: up until now, until this point

examples.en: So far this semester I have not missed a single lecture.
examples.zh: 「到目前为止」这个学期我一节课都没翘。

examples.en: The roommate search is going well so far, with three replies.
examples.zh: 找室友目前进展顺利，「至今」收到三个回复。

words.enDefinition: a large number, used for emphasis

examples.en: There are so many events on campus during welcome week.
examples.zh: 迎新周校园里有「这么多」活动。

examples.en: Why are there so many people in the gym at seven a.m.?
examples.zh: 为什么早上七点健身房有「这么多」人？

words.enDefinition: leave something in liquid to soften or clean it

examples.en: Soak the stained shirt in cold water before you wash it.
examples.zh: 洗之前先把有污渍的衬衫「泡」在冷水里。

examples.en: I left the rice soaking while I went to my morning lecture.
examples.zh: 我去上早课的时候，米饭一直「泡」在水里。

words.enDefinition: a small container that holds a bar of soap

examples.en: I set the soap dish beside the sink so it wouldn't get knocked over.
examples.zh: 我把「肥皂托」放在洗手池旁边，这样不容易被碰翻。

examples.en: My roommate moved the soap dish to make space for another toothbrush cup.
examples.zh: 室友挪开「肥皂托」，腾地方放另一个牙刷杯。

collocations: put soap in the soap dish

words.enDefinition: A container releasing a portion of soap

examples.en: The soap dispenser beside the left sink was empty when I checked.
examples.zh: 我看了一下，左边洗手池旁的「皂液器」空了。

examples.en: The sign pointed to a soap dispenser on the wall between two sinks.
examples.zh: 标牌指向两个洗手池之间的墙上一个「皂液器」。

words.enDefinition: sweet fizzy drink, such as cola or lemon-lime

examples.en: I gave up soda for a month and saved so much money.
examples.zh: 我戒了一个月「汽水」，省下不少钱。

examples.en: Do you want ice and lemon in your soda or not?
examples.zh: 你的「汽水」要不要加冰和柠檬？

words.enDefinition: a non-alcoholic cold drink, usually sweet and fizzy

examples.en: The meal deal lets you pick any soft drink you like.
examples.zh: 套餐可以任选一款「软饮料」。

examples.en: I mostly drink water now, but I used to live on soft drinks.
examples.zh: 我现在主要喝水，以前可是靠「软饮料」过活的。

collocations: a soft drink with the meal

words.enDefinition: a new version that fixes problems or adds features

examples.en: My phone keeps asking for a software update, but I keep postponing it.
examples.zh: 手机一直提醒「软件更新」，我一直拖着不装。

examples.en: The software update wiped my alarm settings, so I overslept on Monday.
examples.zh: 「软件更新」清掉了我设的闹钟，周一就睡过头了。

words.enDefinition: unpleasantly soft and wet from soaking in liquid

examples.en: Leave your cereal too long and it turns completely soggy.
examples.zh: 麦片泡太久就会「泡」得软塌塌的。

examples.en: The fries arrived soggy because the delivery took forty minutes.
examples.zh: 外卖走了四十分钟，薯条送到时已经「软塌塌」的了。

words.enDefinition: on some occasions but not all

examples.en: Sometimes I study better with a bit of background music.
examples.zh: 「有时候」我听着背景音乐学习效果更好。

examples.en: The campus shuttle is sometimes late when it rains really hard.
examples.zh: 雨下得很大时，校园班车「有时」会晚点。

words.enDefinition: at some uncertain future time, eventually

examples.en: Sooner or later you will have to talk to the landlord yourself.
examples.zh: 「迟早」你得亲自和房东谈一次。

examples.en: Sooner or later the free trial ends, so back up your files.
examples.zh: 免费试用「早晚」会到期，记得先备份文件。

words.enDefinition: advanced, complex, and refined in design

examples.en: The library's sophisticated room-booking app even suggests free study spaces near you.
examples.zh: 图书馆「精密」的订座应用还会推荐附近的空位。

examples.en: His surprisingly sophisticated espresso setup makes our tiny shared kitchen feel like a cafe.
examples.zh: 他那套「精良」的意式咖啡设备让我们的小厨房像家咖啡馆。

words.enDefinition: aching and painful when touched or used

examples.en: My legs are really sore after yesterday's gym session with Kai.
examples.zh: 昨天和小凯练完力量，我的腿到现在还是「酸痛」的。

examples.en: I've got a sore throat, so I'm drinking honey lemon water.
examples.zh: 我嗓子「疼」得厉害，只能多喝蜂蜜柠檬水。

words.enDefinition: separate things into groups by type

examples.en: Sort your recycling into the right bins, or the whole building gets fined.
examples.zh: 回收垃圾要「分类」投进对应的桶，不然整栋楼会被罚款。

examples.en: I sorted my emails into folders so scholarship deadlines wouldn't get buried.
examples.zh: 我把邮件「归类」到不同文件夹，免得奖学金的截止日期被淹没。

words.enDefinition: in some way but not exactly

examples.en: The movie was sort of boring, but the popcorn was great.
examples.zh: 电影「有点」无聊，不过爆米花很好吃。

examples.en: I sort of promised my roommate I'd clean the bathroom today.
examples.zh: 我「算是」答应过室友今天打扫卫生间。

words.enDefinition: make a confusing situation organized and solved

examples.en: Give me an hour to sort out these receipts and bills.
examples.zh: 给我一个小时把这些收据和账单「理清」。

examples.en: We sorted out the schedule problem with one quick phone call.
examples.zh: 我们打了个简短的电话就把日程问题「解决」了。

words.enDefinition: to look through a group of things carefully to find, check or organize them

examples.en: I had to sort through three folders before finding the lecturer's handout.
examples.zh: 找到讲师的讲义前，我得在三个文件夹里「逐一翻找筛选」。

examples.en: We spent the morning trying to sort through the boxes from our move.
examples.zh: 我们上午试着在搬家带来的那些箱子里「逐一翻找筛选」。

collocations: help someone sort through the boxes

words.enDefinition: sleeping deeply and peacefully

examples.en: My roommate was sound asleep, so I tiptoed in with the lights off.
examples.zh: 室友「睡得正香」，我关着灯踮脚进去的。

examples.en: Don't call him at noon; he's usually sound asleep after his night shift.
examples.zh: 中午别给他打电话，上完夜班的他通常「睡得正香」。

words.enDefinition: built so that sound cannot pass through

examples.en: The music rooms are soundproof, so band practice runs until midnight.
examples.zh: 琴房「隔音」很好，乐队排练能到半夜。

examples.en: I wish our dorm walls were soundproof; I hear every karaoke night.
examples.zh: 真希望宿舍墙能「隔音」，隔壁的 K 歌之夜我全听见了。

words.enDefinition: a milk-like drink made from soybeans

examples.en: I add soy milk to my latte because dairy upsets my stomach.
examples.zh: 我拿铁里加「豆奶」，因为乳制品让肠胃不舒服。

examples.en: The cafe near campus charges nothing extra for swapping in soy milk.
examples.zh: 校园附近这家咖啡馆换「豆奶」不加钱。

words.enDefinition: large inside, with plenty of room to move

examples.en: The shared kitchen is surprisingly spacious, so four of us cook together.
examples.zh: 公共厨房意外地「宽敞」，我们四个人能一起做饭。

examples.en: This studio looks spacious because the bed folds into the wall.
examples.zh: 这间开间看着「宽敞」，因为床可以折进墙里。

words.enDefinition: an unwanted call from telemarketers or recorded robots

examples.en: I get a spam call about student loans at least twice a week.
examples.zh: 我每周至少接到两个关于学生贷款的「骚扰电话」。

examples.en: Answering one spam call apparently signs you up for five more.
examples.zh: 据说接了一个「骚扰电话」，之后就会有五个打进来。

words.enDefinition: A seat available for someone else to use

examples.en: I saw a spare seat near the wall and moved closer to the group.
examples.zh: 我看到墙边有个「空余座位」，就往小组那边挪了挪。

examples.en: The volunteer pointed out a spare seat at the end of the front row.
examples.zh: 志愿者指了指出第一排最边上的一个「空余座位」。

collocations: a spare seat at the back

words.enDefinition: free time left over after classes, work, and daily duties

examples.en: In my spare time I volunteer at the campus food bank.
examples.zh: 「空闲时间」我会去校内食物银行做志愿者。

examples.en: She tutors math in her spare time to cover living costs.
examples.zh: 她利用「空闲时间」做数学家教，补贴生活费。

words.enDefinition: raise your voice so people can hear you

examples.en: Could you speak up? The music here is really loud.
examples.zh: 你能「大声一点」吗？这里的音乐声太大了。

examples.en: Grandpa asked me to speak up during our phone call.
examples.zh: 爷爷让我打电话时「说大声些」。

collocations: speak up in a noisy place

words.enDefinition: a mode that plays a call out loud without holding the phone

examples.en: Put the clinic on speakerphone so we can both hear the appointment options.
examples.zh: 把诊所来电开「免提」，这样咱俩都能听到预约选项。

examples.en: My roommate takes every call on speakerphone, which drives me crazy during naps.
examples.zh: 我室友打电话全开「免提」，我午睡时简直受不了。

words.enDefinition: move faster, or make something move faster

examples.en: Speed up a little if you want to catch the 8:05 shuttle.
examples.zh: 想赶 8:05 的校车，就稍微「加快脚步」。

examples.en: My walking pace speeds up automatically near the dining hall at noon.
examples.zh: 中午快到食堂时，我的脚步会不自觉「加快」。

words.enDefinition: turn quickly in one spot in a full circle

examples.en: Spin around once and point; that's how we pick who washes dishes.
examples.zh: 「转个圈」然后随手一指——我们就是这样决定谁洗碗的。

examples.en: I saw my roommate spin around when someone knocked loudly at the front door.
examples.zh: 有人用力敲大门时，我看见室友「猛地转身」。

words.enDefinition: the fast spinning part that removes water from clothes

examples.en: The spin cycle is so loud in our basement that it shakes the walls.
examples.zh: 地下室的「脱水程序」声音大得能震墙。

examples.en: Add an extra spin cycle if the jeans come out still dripping.
examples.zh: 如果牛仔裤拿出来还在滴水，就再加一次「脱水」。

words.enDefinition: divide housework fairly between roommates or family

examples.en: Let's split the chores: I'll take the bathroom, you take the kitchen floor.
examples.zh: 我们「分摊家务」吧：我负责浴室，你负责厨房地板。

examples.en: We split the chores fairly, so nobody feels like the housekeeper.
examples.zh: 我们公平地「分摊家务」，没人觉得自己像保姆。

words.enDefinition: no longer good to eat because it went bad

examples.en: The milk smelled spoiled even though the date said three more days.
examples.zh: 牛奶闻着「变味」了，可保质期明明还剩三天。

examples.en: A spoiled tomato at the bottom of the bag ruined the others.
examples.zh: 袋子底下一个「坏」番茄，把其他的都带坏了。

words.enDefinition: to remove dirt or a mark by wiping with a damp sponge

examples.en: I tried to sponge off the muddy marks before they dried on the bag.
examples.zh: 泥印还没干在包上，我就试着「用海绵擦掉」。

examples.en: My roommate helped me sponge off the dust left on the plastic chairs.
examples.zh: 室友帮我「用海绵擦掉」塑料椅上留下的灰。

collocations: use water to sponge off the residue

words.enDefinition: a flavored drink that replaces salts after exercise

examples.en: Coach hands out sports drinks after every long practice session.
examples.zh: 每次大强度训练后教练都会发「运动饮料」。

examples.en: For a one-hour gym session, water beats any sports drink.
examples.zh: 一小时以内的健身，白水比任何「运动饮料」都好。

collocations: water instead of a sports drink

words.enDefinition: perfectly clean, with no dirt at all

examples.en: My roommate scrubbed the kitchen until it was completely spotless.
examples.zh: 室友把厨房擦得「一尘不染」。

examples.en: Landlords expect the flat spotless when you hand back the keys.
examples.zh: 退房交钥匙时，房东要求屋子「一尘不染」。

words.enDefinition: an internet connection that keeps cutting in and out

examples.en: The spotty connection in the basement kicked me off the online quiz twice.
examples.zh: 地下室「网络不稳定」，我两次被踢下线，线上测验都做不了。

examples.en: A spotty connection makes video calls sound like a robot voice.
examples.zh: 「网络不稳定」的时候，视频通话听起来像机器人在说话。

collocations: a spotty connection in the basement

words.enDefinition: lie or sit stretched out with limbs spread wide

examples.en: He sprawled across the common-room couch right after his last final exam.
examples.zh: 最后一门期末考试一结束，他就「四仰八叉地躺」在活动室沙发上。

examples.en: Don't sprawl over two seats when the lounge is that crowded.
examples.zh: 休息室这么挤，别一个人「摊」占两个位子。

words.enDefinition: tell other people unverified stories about someone

examples.en: Someone spread rumors about a dorm inspection, and half the floor panicked.
examples.zh: 有人「散布谣言」说宿舍要检查，半层楼的人都慌了。

examples.en: Spreading rumors about roommates can destroy trust on a whole floor.
examples.zh: 「传室友的谣言」可能毁掉一整层楼的信任。

words.enDefinition: thorough cleaning of a home, traditionally done in spring

examples.en: I'm doing some spring cleaning and found clothes I forgot I owned.
examples.zh: 我在做「春季大扫除」，翻出了自己都忘了的衣服。

examples.en: Our dorm tradition is a big spring cleaning right after finals week.
examples.zh: 我们宿舍的传统是期末周一结束就来一场「春季大扫除」。

words.enDefinition: scatter small drops or pieces lightly over something

examples.en: Sprinkle some cheese on top before you bake the pasta.
examples.zh: 烤意面前在表面「撒」点芝士。

examples.en: She sprinkled chili powder over the fries at the dining hall.
examples.zh: 食堂里她往薯条上「撒」了点辣椒粉。

words.enDefinition: run at full speed for a short distance

examples.en: Sprint to the lecture hall if you leave the library after 9:55.
examples.zh: 九点五十五才出图书馆的话，就得「冲刺」去教室了。

examples.en: He sprinted the last two blocks to make the mail cutoff.
examples.zh: 为了赶上邮局最后一班收件，他最后两个街区一路「狂奔」。

words.enDefinition: lower your body by bending your knees fully down

examples.en: Squat down to check under the vending machine for your coin.
examples.zh: 硬币掉进自动售货机底下，得「蹲下」看。

examples.en: He squatted beside his suitcase to repack it in the hallway.
examples.zh: 他在走廊里「蹲」在行李箱旁重新装箱。

words.enDefinition: making a short high noise when moved or pressed

examples.en: My desk chair is so squeaky that everyone turns around in the library.
examples.zh: 我的椅子「吱嘎」响得厉害，在图书馆里人人都回头。

examples.en: The squeaky door hinge needs a drop of oil before the neighbors complain.
examples.zh: 趁邻居还没投诉，先给「吱嘎」响的合页滴几滴油。

words.enDefinition: manage to fit something into a busy schedule

examples.en: I squeezed in a gym session between my two lectures.
examples.zh: 我在两节课之间「挤出时间」去了趟健身房。

examples.en: Can you squeeze in a quick call with me before dinner?
examples.zh: 晚饭前你能「抽空」和我快速通个话吗？

words.enDefinition: get past through a narrow gap by pressing sideways

examples.en: Squeeze through the gap between the shelves; it's faster than the main aisle.
examples.zh: 从货架间的缝隙「挤过去」，比走主通道快。

examples.en: I squeezed through the packed crowd near the stage to find my friends.
examples.zh: 我从舞台前「挤过」密集人群去找朋友。

words.enDefinition: look at something with your eyes partly closed

examples.en: I squint at the whiteboard from the back row; the marker is too thin.
examples.zh: 坐后排看白板我得「眯着眼」，马克笔笔迹太细了。

examples.en: He squinted at the tiny print on the bus schedule.
examples.zh: 公交时刻表的字太小，他「眯起眼」看了半天。

words.enDefinition: arrange things in a neat pile

examples.en: Stack the clean dishes on the drying rack instead of putting them away wet.
examples.zh: 洗好的碗先「摞」在沥水架上，别湿着放回橱柜。

examples.en: She stacked her borrowed library books neatly by the door.
examples.zh: 她把借来的图书馆的书整齐地「码」在门边。

words.enDefinition: For use by employees or designated workers only

examples.en: The sign said “Staff only,” so I went back to the public entrance.
examples.zh: 牌子上写着「仅限工作人员」，我就回到了公众入口。

examples.en: A “Staff only” notice was on the door leading from the hall to the kitchen.
examples.zh: 从大厅通往厨房的门上贴着「仅限工作人员」的告示。

words.enDefinition: walk unsteadily as if you might fall over

examples.en: People stagger out of the 8 a.m. final looking completely drained.
examples.zh: 早八期末考出来的人都「步履踉跄」，一脸虚脱。

examples.en: I staggered under the weight of four full grocery bags.
examples.zh: 四大袋食品压得我走路都「摇摇晃晃」。

words.enDefinition: a product you apply to spots before washing

examples.en: Dab some stain remover on the coffee spot before it dries.
examples.zh: 趁咖啡渍还没干，赶紧涂点「去渍剂」。

examples.en: A travel-size stain remover lives in my backpack for emergencies.
examples.zh: 我背包里常备一支旅行装的「去渍剂」应急。

collocations: apply stain remover to the spot

words.enDefinition: marked by spots that are hard to wash out

examples.en: The white shirt came back from the wash still stained with coffee.
examples.zh: 白衬衫洗完回来还是「沾着」咖啡渍。

examples.en: We lost part of the deposit over a stained mattress.
examples.zh: 床垫「有污渍」，押金被扣了一部分。

words.enDefinition: A level space between or at the end of stairs

examples.en: We paused on the stair landing so a group could pass us on their way down.
examples.zh: 我们在「楼梯平台」停了一下，让一群下楼的人先过去。

examples.en: A window on the stair landing let in afternoon light from the courtyard.
examples.zh: 「楼梯平台」上的窗户让午后的阳光从院子照进来。

collocations: a window at the stair landing

words.enDefinition: no longer fresh, hard or dry as a result

examples.en: The free-box bagels had gone stale, but toasting fixed them.
examples.zh: 免费箱里的贝果已经「不新鲜」了，烤一下还能吃。

examples.en: Stale chips at the bottom of the bag are a student rite of passage.
examples.zh: 吃到最后袋底那些「走了气」的薯片，算是学生的必修课。

words.enDefinition: fail to show up at an arranged meeting

examples.en: He stood me up at the cinema and never texted back.
examples.zh: 他「放了我鸽子」，人没到电影院，消息也不回。

examples.en: She was stood up once and never forgot how it felt.
examples.zh: 她「被放鸽子」过一次，一直没忘记那种滋味。

collocations: stand someone up on a date

words.enDefinition: Having room to stand but no seats left

examples.en: The hall was standing room only by the time we arrived after class.
examples.zh: 我们下课赶到大厅时，「只剩站位」了。

examples.en: A volunteer warned us that the reading would be standing room only by noon.
examples.zh: 志愿者提醒我们，到中午朗读活动就会「只剩站位」。

collocations: end up with standing room only

words.enDefinition: begin your daily activities, usually in the morning

examples.en: I like to start my day with a quick shower and a coffee.
examples.zh: 我喜欢先冲个澡、喝杯咖啡，这样「开始一天」。

examples.en: Stretching for five minutes is a calm way to start the day.
examples.zh: 花五分钟拉伸一下，是平静地「开启一天」的方式。

collocations: a good way to start the day

words.enDefinition: to keep drinking enough water during the day

examples.en: Drink water regularly — you need to stay hydrated in this heat.
examples.zh: 天这么热，要常喝水「保持水分」。

examples.en: The trainer reminded us to stay hydrated during two-a-day practices.
examples.zh: 教练提醒我们一天两练期间要「补充水分」。

words.enDefinition: remain at home instead of going out socially

examples.en: I'm staying in tonight to catch up on my laundry and sleep.
examples.zh: 今晚我「待在家里」，补一下洗衣和睡眠。

examples.en: We stayed in and watched movies instead of going to the party.
examples.zh: 我们「待在家里」看电影，没去派对。

words.enDefinition: remain outside home until very late at night

examples.en: We stayed out late celebrating her birthday and regretted it at 8 a.m. class.
examples.zh: 我们庆祝她生日「在外面玩到很晚」，早八的课真是后悔。

examples.en: Don't stay out late tonight; the last subway leaves at midnight.
examples.zh: 今晚别「在外面待到很晚」，末班地铁十二点就发车。

collocations: never stay out late on weekdays

words.enDefinition: remain awake much later than usual

examples.en: I stayed up finishing the essay and felt awful today.
examples.zh: 我「熬夜」赶完了论文，今天难受极了。

examples.en: Don't stay up chatting, we have an early class tomorrow.
examples.zh: 别「熬夜」聊天了，明天一早我们有课。

words.enDefinition: regular, continuous, and not changing suddenly

examples.en: A steady weekend job at the campus bookstore covers my phone bill and coffee.
examples.zh: 校书店一份「稳定」的周末工作够我付话费和咖啡钱。

examples.en: His steady progress in speaking came from practicing with the language partner program daily.
examples.zh: 他口语「稳步」进步，靠的是每天参加语伴项目练习。

words.enDefinition: To move to one side of a space

examples.en: I had to step aside when the volunteer came through with a stack of chairs.
examples.zh: 志愿者搬着一摞椅子过来时，我得「往旁边站开」。

examples.en: Could you step aside for a moment so I can get past with these chairs?
examples.zh: 你能「往旁边站开」一下，让我搬着这些椅子过去吗？

collocations: step aside to let someone pass

words.enDefinition: the son of your step-parent, not related by blood

examples.en: My stepbrother is a sophomore here, so we grab lunch sometimes.
examples.zh: 我的「继兄弟」就在这所学校读大二，所以我们有时会一起吃午饭。

examples.en: I share a room with my stepbrother when I visit my dad.
examples.zh: 回爸爸家的时候，我和「继弟」睡同一个房间。

collocations: share a room with my stepbrother

words.enDefinition: the daughter of your husband or wife from an earlier marriage

examples.en: Her stepdaughter studies art, so they visit the museum together.
examples.zh: 她的「继女」学艺术，所以她们常常一起逛博物馆。

examples.en: The professor mentioned his stepdaughter during the campus family day.
examples.zh: 校园家庭日上，教授提到了他的「继女」。

words.enDefinition: your mother's new husband after a divorce or remarriage

examples.en: My stepfather taught me how to drive in the empty parking lot.
examples.zh: 「继父」在空旷的停车场教我开车。

examples.en: I call my stepfather by his first name, and he doesn't mind.
examples.zh: 我直呼「继父」的名字，他也并不介意。

words.enDefinition: your father's new wife after a divorce or remarriage

examples.en: My stepmother picked me up from the airport when my dad was busy.
examples.zh: 爸爸没空的时候，是「继母」来机场接的我。

examples.en: It took a year, but my stepmother and I finally get along well.
examples.zh: 虽然花了一年时间，但我和「继母」终于相处得很好。

words.enDefinition: the daughter of your step-parent, not related by blood

examples.en: My stepsister helped me choose courses before the semester started.
examples.zh: 开学前，「继姐」帮我选好了课。

examples.en: My stepsister and I text almost every day even though we live apart.
examples.zh: 虽然住得远，我和「继妹」几乎每天都发消息。

words.enDefinition: the son of your husband or wife from an earlier marriage

examples.en: My uncle's stepson joined us for Thanksgiving dinner this year.
examples.zh: 今年感恩节，我叔叔的「继子」和我们一起吃了晚饭。

examples.en: Our host family introduced us to their teenage stepson at dinner.
examples.zh: 晚饭时，寄宿家庭向我们介绍了他们十几岁的「继子」。

words.enDefinition: a larger cartoon image sent in chats for fun

examples.en: My grandma sends me the same cute sticker twenty times a day.
examples.zh: 我奶奶一天能给我发二十次同一个可爱「表情贴纸」。

examples.en: There is a whole sticker pack for finals week with crying cats in it.
examples.zh: 有个考试周专属的「表情贴纸」包，里面全是哭泣的猫。

words.enDefinition: not able to bend or move easily and comfortably

examples.en: Sitting through three back-to-back lectures left my neck really stiff.
examples.zh: 连着上了三节课，我的脖子都「僵」了。

examples.en: New leather shoes always feel stiff until you break them in.
examples.zh: 新皮鞋一开始都「硬邦邦」的，穿一阵子才会合脚。

words.enDefinition: unwilling to spend or share money

examples.en: My landlord is so stingy that he refuses to fix the heating properly.
examples.zh: 我房东「小气」得很，都不肯好好修暖气。

examples.en: Don't be stingy with the cheese; we already bought a whole bag.
examples.zh: 芝士别放得那么「抠」，我们可是买了一整袋。

words.enDefinition: buy a large amount of something for later use

examples.en: Let's stock up on noodles before the storm arrives tonight.
examples.zh: 今晚暴风雨来之前，我们多「囤」些泡面。

examples.en: I stocked up on snacks and drinks for our movie night.
examples.zh: 电影之夜前我「囤了」不少零食和饮料。

words.enDefinition: visit a place or person briefly on your way

examples.en: I'll stop by the post office after class to mail this package.
examples.zh: 下课后我会「顺路去趟」邮局寄这个包裹。

examples.en: Stop by my office anytime if the schedule still confuses you.
examples.zh: 如果课表还是让你犯迷糊，随时「来」我办公室坐坐。

words.enDefinition: A small open compartment used for storing belongings

examples.en: I slid my backpack into a storage cubby before taking a seat in the hall.
examples.zh: 我先把背包塞进一个「开放式储物格」，再在大厅找了个座位。

examples.en: The storage cubby by the door was wide enough for my bike helmet.
examples.zh: 门旁的「开放式储物格」够宽，能放下我的自行车头盔。

collocations: place a bag in a storage cubby

words.enDefinition: leave a room suddenly and visibly angry

examples.en: She stormed out of the group meeting after the second argument.
examples.zh: 第二次争执后，她「气冲冲地」离开了小组会。

examples.en: My flatmate stormed out over the thermostat argument, then returned for his charger.
examples.zh: 室友为空调温度之争「愤然摔门而去」，又回来拿充电器。

collocations: slam the door and storm out

words.enDefinition: make a room tidy by putting things in place

examples.en: I straighten up my desk every evening so mornings feel less chaotic.
examples.zh: 我每天晚上都会把书桌「收拾整齐」，早上就不会乱糟糟。

examples.en: Let's straighten up the living room before the study group arrives.
examples.zh: 学习小组来之前，我们把客厅「收拾一下吧」。

words.enDefinition: honest and direct about what you think

examples.en: My supervisor is straightforward, so I always know where I stand.
examples.zh: 我的导师「直截了当」，所以我清楚自己所处的位置。

examples.en: Just be straightforward and tell your roommate the dishes bother you.
examples.zh: 有话就「直说」，直接告诉室友碗筷的事让你不舒服。

words.enDefinition: a person you do not know at all

examples.en: My mom taught me never to share my address with strangers.
examples.zh: 妈妈从小教我，不要把住址告诉「陌生人」。

examples.en: A kind stranger helped me carry my suitcases up the station stairs.
examples.zh: 一位好心的「陌生人」帮我把行李箱抬上了车站的楼梯。

words.enDefinition: a thin tube used for drinking cold drinks

examples.en: The boba shop near campus uses paper straws now instead of plastic.
examples.zh: 校园附近的奶茶店现在改用纸质「吸管」了。

examples.en: Can I get a straw for this iced coffee, please?
examples.zh: 这杯冰咖啡能给我一根「吸管」吗？

words.enDefinition: needing a lot of physical effort and energy

examples.en: Nothing strenuous after the flu shot, the nurse said, so I just walked.
examples.zh: 护士说打完流感疫苗别做「剧烈」运动，于是我只散了步。

examples.en: The trail got strenuous halfway up, and we stopped for water.
examples.zh: 爬到半山腰那段特别「费劲」，我们停下来补水。

words.enDefinition: feeling very tense and unable to relax because of pressure

examples.en: I've been so stressed out about finals that I can't sleep properly.
examples.zh: 期末临近，我一直「压力很大」，觉都睡不好。

examples.en: My roommate gets stressed out every time she checks her budget.
examples.zh: 每次一查自己的预算，室友就「压力山大」。

words.enDefinition: able to stretch and return to its shape

examples.en: These stretchy gym leggings survive every squat without going see-through.
examples.zh: 这条「弹力好」的健身裤深蹲也不会变透。

examples.en: Wear something stretchy for the long flight; jeans get uncomfortable.
examples.zh: 长途飞机穿「有弹性」的裤子吧，牛仔裤坐着难受。

words.enDefinition: walk with long, confident steps

examples.en: We watched her stride into the room ten minutes early, looking cheerful and relaxed.
examples.zh: 我们看着她提前十分钟「大步走进」房间，神态轻松愉快。

examples.en: Stride across campus like you know exactly where the seminar is.
examples.zh: 在校园里「大步走」，显得你完全清楚研讨课在哪儿。

words.enDefinition: very noticeable and catching attention at once

examples.en: The photo exhibit shows a striking contrast between campus life in 1990 and today.
examples.zh: 摄影展里1990年与如今的校园生活形成「引人注目」的对比。

examples.en: Her striking red coat made her easy to spot in the crowded station.
examples.zh: 她那件「引人注目」的红大衣让我在拥挤的车站一眼认出她。

words.enDefinition: walk slowly in a relaxed way for pleasure

examples.en: We strolled along the river path after submitting the group report.
examples.zh: 交完小组报告，我们沿着河边步道「溜达」。

examples.en: Stroll through the farmers market on Saturday if you want cheap fruit.
examples.zh: 想买便宜水果，周六可以「逛逛」农贸市场。

words.enDefinition: refusing to change your mind even when wrong

examples.en: My dad is too stubborn to ask for directions even with GPS on.
examples.zh: 我爸「固执」得很，开着导航也不肯问路。

examples.en: She's stubborn about her thesis topic, even after the advisor objected.
examples.zh: 导师提出异议后，她对论文选题依然很「固执」。

words.enDefinition: unable to move because the roads are crowded

examples.en: Sorry I'm late, I was stuck in traffic on the bridge for an hour.
examples.zh: 抱歉我迟到了，我在桥上「堵了一个小时」。

examples.en: Leave early, because you never know when you'll get stuck in traffic.
examples.zh: 早点出门吧，谁知道什么时候会「堵在路上」。

collocations: stuck in traffic for an hour

words.enDefinition: feeling uncomfortably full from eating too much

examples.en: I'm so stuffed from the all-you-can-eat hotpot that I can barely walk.
examples.zh: 自助火锅吃得太狠，我「撑」得快走不动了。

examples.en: Don't order more noodles; I'm already stuffed after that huge lunch.
examples.zh: 别再加面了，午餐那顿我已经吃得很「撑」。

words.enDefinition: warm and close, with no fresh air moving

examples.en: Open a window; the study room gets stuffy by mid-afternoon.
examples.zh: 开扇窗吧，自习室一到下午就「闷」了。

examples.en: I almost fell asleep because the lecture hall was so stuffy.
examples.zh: 阶梯教室「闷」得我差点睡着。

words.enDefinition: put your foot down awkwardly and almost fall

examples.en: People stumble on that loose step by the science building all the time.
examples.zh: 理科楼那级松动的台阶，总让人「绊一下」。

examples.en: She stumbled over the doormat while carrying her laundry basket.
examples.zh: 抱着洗衣篮时，她被门口的地垫「绊了个趔趄」。

words.enDefinition: extremely beautiful or impressively attractive

examples.en: My roommate looked stunning in her dress at the international culture night.
examples.zh: 国际文化之夜上，室友的礼服造型十分「惊艳」。

examples.en: The wedding photos came out stunning even though it rained all morning.
examples.zh: 虽然下了一上午的雨，婚纱照还是拍得「惊艳」。

words.enDefinition: strong and well made, not easily broken

examples.en: Buy a sturdy umbrella here; the cheap ones die in one storm.
examples.zh: 在这儿买把「结实」的伞，便宜的撑不过一场暴雨。

examples.en: You'll need sturdy shelves to hold all these engineering textbooks.
examples.zh: 这些工科教材很沉，得用「结实」的书架才放得住。

words.enDefinition: attractive in a way that shows good modern taste

examples.en: A thrifted blazer looks surprisingly stylish with plain jeans and sneakers.
examples.zh: 二手西装外套配素色牛仔裤和小白鞋，会意外地「时髦」。

examples.en: Our TA manages to stay stylish even in a baggy lab coat.
examples.zh: 助教哪怕套着宽松的实验服也照样「有型」。

words.enDefinition: the short title at the top of an email

examples.en: Put your course code in the subject line so the professor finds your email fast.
examples.zh: 在「邮件主题」里写上课号，教授就能更快找到你的邮件。

examples.en: A clear subject line like 'Question about Essay 2' gets replies sooner.
examples.zh: 像“Essay 2 的问题”这样清楚的「邮件主题」，能更快得到回复。

words.enDefinition: based on personal feelings rather than facts

examples.en: Taste in music is totally subjective, so we stopped arguing about each other's playlists.
examples.zh: 音乐品味完全是「主观」的，我们就不互相吐槽歌单了。

examples.en: Grading art projects is subjective, which is why the professor shares a detailed rubric.
examples.zh: 艺术作业打分很「主观」，所以教授公布了详细的评分标准。

words.enDefinition: below the usual expected standard

examples.en: The Wi-Fi in my dorm is subpar, so I do my uploads in the library.
examples.zh: 宿舍的Wi-Fi「不达标」，要传文件我都去图书馆。

examples.en: Customer service at that phone company was subpar when I tried to cancel my plan.
examples.zh: 我去那家运营商取消套餐，客服服务实在「不达标」。

words.enDefinition: made with no added sugar at all

examples.en: I keep sugar-free gum in my bag for long library days.
examples.zh: 我包里备着「无糖」口香糖，泡图书馆的日子用。

examples.en: These sugar-free cookies still taste surprisingly sweet to me somehow.
examples.zh: 这些「无糖」饼干吃起来不知怎么还是挺甜的。

words.enDefinition: the jacket made to match the other pieces of a suit

examples.en: I kept the suit jacket with its matching trousers until the morning of my presentation.
examples.zh: 汇报当天早上之前，我一直把「套装中的西装上衣」和配套西裤放在一起。

examples.en: My suit jacket was over the back of my chair after the award ceremony.
examples.zh: 颁奖典礼结束后，我的「套装中的西装上衣」搭在椅背上。

words.enDefinition: bright with sunlight and few clouds

examples.en: It is sunny all week, so the quad will be packed.
examples.zh: 整周都是「晴天」，草坪上肯定全是人。

examples.en: The sunny weather finally lifted everyone's mood right before finals.
examples.zh: 期末前的「晴朗」天气让所有人的心情都好了起来。

words.enDefinition: cream that protects skin from strong sun

examples.en: Remember to apply sunscreen before the noon beach volleyball practice.
examples.zh: 正午沙滩排球训练前，记得涂好「防晒霜」。

examples.en: The campus pharmacy sells sunscreen cheaper than the corner store.
examples.zh: 校内药店卖的「防晒霜」比街角商店便宜。

words.enDefinition: the time in the evening when the sun disappears

examples.en: We watched the sunset from the library roof after the barbecue.
examples.zh: 烧烤结束后，我们在图书馆屋顶看了「日落」。

examples.en: Sunset is around eight in summer, so the evenings feel long.
examples.zh: 夏天「日落」大约在八点，所以夜晚感觉很长。

words.enDefinition: only on the surface, without depth

examples.en: Their superficial small talk never got beyond weather, majors, and weekend plans.
examples.zh: 他们的闲聊「浮于表面」，话题从没超出天气、专业和周末安排。

examples.en: The draft gave a superficial overview of the issue without citing a single study.
examples.zh: 初稿对问题的梳理「很肤浅」，一项研究都没引用。

words.enDefinition: an informal word for the evening meal in some families

examples.en: We usually have supper around six at my host family's place.
examples.zh: 在寄宿家庭，我们通常六点左右吃「晚饭」。

examples.en: Grandma kept supper warm for me even though I got home late.
examples.zh: 虽然我到家晚了，奶奶还是帮我留着「晚饭」。

words.enDefinition: always ready to help and encourage others

examples.en: My parents were supportive when I chose an arts major.
examples.zh: 我选艺术专业时，父母非常「支持」我。

examples.en: A supportive roommate makes homesickness much easier to deal with.
